against they these thing in time will much avail we be well observe and right apply according to occasion but to our former discourse the power and strength of these country be so thin people be not very great to withstand the might of foreign enemy the usual weapon of the indian be before describe save that their arrow be oft time poison but since our trade and commerce with they they have get a few good sword musket caliver and some small quantity of shot and powder and have learned to handle their piece very orderly and some of they be good shot the season of the year upon this coast and in this climate be diverse for in the east part of Guiana towards the amazon the dry weather which we call their summer begin in August the season of the year in Guiana the summer begin in August the winter begin in February and the violent reins and tempestuous wind which we count their winter do begin in February but in the western part towards Orenoque the dry season begin in October and the reins and wind in April there be little difference of heat and cold in this diversity of season be so near the equinoctial where the day and night be always equal for in those part we find that when the sun decline further from they towards the tropic of Capricorn the air be then clear and the season of the year most dry as in the eastern part of Guiana in August September October November and December and when the sun return towards the tropic of cancer then do the reins begin increase and decrease from Frbruary to july but sometime they begin to fall and the river to rise swell and overflow soon or late by a month and the year be sometime more or less windy and wet according to the disposition of the heaven and of the planet and as the sun approach or decline little or much even so the earth want or abound with water and moisture they have no division or account of time or number they only reckon by the moon as their account of time and number one two three four or five moon or by day in like manner their number they reckon thus one two three and so to ten then they say ten and one ten and two ten and three etc. and to show their meaning more certain they will hold up one two three or more of their finger express the number still make sign as they speak the better to declare their meaning when they will reckon twenty they will hold down both their hand to their foot show all their finger and toe and as the number be great so will they double the sign when they appoint or promise any thing to be do by a time limit they will deliver a little bundle of stick equal to the number of day or moon that they appoint and will themselves keep another bundle of the like number and to observe their appoint time they will every day or moon take away a stick and when they have take away all than they know that the time of their appointment be come and will according perform their promise as touch religion they have none among they that I can perceive more than a certain religion they use no sacrifice not religious worship to any thing observance of the sun and moon suppose they to be alive but use no religious worship towards they nor offer sacrifice to any thing unless they use a superstition in their drink feast by sacrifice jar of drink for at the death of any of their cassique captain or great friend who they esteem they will make a solemn feast their chief provision be of their best and strong drink which they call Parranow which feast shall the manner of their drink feast at the death of their captain continue three or four day or as long as their liquor last spend their time in dance sing and drink excessive in which vice they exceed all other nation whatsoever account he that will be drink first the brave fellow during this solemnity of their drink some woman be near of their kin unto the party dead do stand by and cry extreme thus their manner be until their drink be spend and then the feast be end whether they use any superstition in this custom I know not time will reveal and also reform it it be most certain that their peeaios as they call they priest or soothsayer at some special their peeaios or priest have conference with the devil their opinion of the dead at the death of a cassique they kill a indian to serve he in the other world time have conference with the devil the common deceiver of mankind who they call Wattipa and be by he delude yet not withstand their often conference with he they fear and hate he much and say that he be nought and not without great reason for he will oftentimes to their great terror beat they black and blue they believe that the good indian when they die go up and will point towards the heaven which they call Caupo and that the bad indian go down point to the earth which they call when any cassique captain or chief man die among they if he have a slave or prisoner take from their enemy they will kill he and if he have none such then will they kill one of his other servant that he may have one to attend he in the other world the quality of the land in those country be of diverse kind by the sea side the land be low where the heat will be most vehement if it be not qualify and temper by a the quality of the Land fresh easterly wind or breeze most forcible blow in the heat of the day in many place this low land be very unhealthful and little inhabit by reason of the overflow of the water but for the most part it have goodly navigable river a fertile soil much people and be a healthful habitation upon the mountain there be a high land where the air be cold in some place it be fruitful in other not but general be full of mineral and mine of metal and yield as many as any part either of the east or west indies both of the best and of the base whereof we shall by God permission give good testimony to the benefit of our country and honour of our nation in time convenient and in most place upon the mountain there be sound and healthful dwell there be also a middle sort of land which be of a mean height and be most temperate healthful fertile and most inhabit of all other it abound in meadow pasture and pleasant stream of fresh water in goodly wood and most delightful plain for profit pleasure sport and recreation and also be not void of mineral the provision of this country for victual be many first of the root of a tree call the provision for victual the root of Cassavi make their bread and drink Cassavi they make their bread in manner follow they grate the root upon a stone and press out the juice thereof which be raw be poison but boil with Guinea pepper whereof they have abundance it make a excellent and wholesome sauce than they dry the grate root and bake it upon a stone as we bake our oaten cake in England this bread be very excellent much like but far better than our great oaten cake a finger thick which be use in the moorelands and the Peake in Staffordshire and Darbyshire there be a kind of great wheat call Maix of some it be call Guinea wheat which grain be a singular provision in those country and yield admirable increase even a thousand or fifteen or Guinea wheat hundred for one and many time much more it make excellent meal or flower for bread and very good malt for beer or ale and serve well for sundry other necessary use for the relief of man of the aforesaid Cassavi bread and this England by sir Walter Raleigh the several kind of fruit be many the Pina Platana potato Medler plum of diverse sundry kind a of fruit Pina fort the nut of strange kind the excellency of the Pina I can Platana potato M^dler plum the potato be well know the Medler exceed in greatness the plum I can commend for to eat much of they do cause flux which in those country be dangerous the nut be good be moderate eat have thus most excellent prince declare the several sort of provision for victual and nut necessary foode it remain that I now make mention of the variety of commodity find in the country for the trade of merchandise which in few year by our pain and industry may be bring to perfection and so settle in those part that not only the undertaker may receive reward for their endeavour but our country also may grow rich by trade for the fruit of our labour the first and principal commodity of estimation be the sugarcane whereof in those part the variety of commodity sugar cane there be great plenty the soil be as fertile for they as in any other part of the world they do there grow to great bigness in a short time by orderly and fit plant of they and by erect convenient work for the boil and make of sugar which at the first will require some charge and expense may be yearly return great benefit and wealth the long experience of the portugal and spaniard in brasil and the island of the canary and of the moor in Barbary may give we certain assurance and full satisfaction thereof the cotton wool be a general commodity beneficial to our merchant and profitable to Cotton wool our country by make of fustian and serve for bombast and other use for make of Hamaccas which be the indian bed most necessary in those part and also of a fine cotton cloth for clothing of the people there be a natural hemp or flax of great use almost as fine natural hemp or flax cloth it be most excellent there be many rare and singular commodity for dyer of which sort there be a red berry diverse commodity for dyer Annoto call Annoto which be right prepare by the indian die a perfect and sure orange-tawnie in silk it have be sell in Holland for twelve shilling starling the pound and be yet of a good price there be another berry that die blue there be also a gum of a tree whereof I have see experience that in cloth die a sure and perfect yellow in grain there be a gum which die a yellow in grain leaf of certain tree which be right prepare do die a deep red there be also a wood which die a purple and be of a good price and another that die yellow there be yet another wood which die a purple when the liquor be hot and a crimson when the liquor be cold many other notable thing there be no doubt not yet know unto we which by our diligent labour and observation in time will be discover and find the sweet gum of inestimable value and strange operation in physic and chirurgery be innumerable there be yellow amber Lemnia Colliman or Carriman Barratta and many more which I omit the Collman have be prove by master Walter Cary of Wictham sweet gum in buckinghamshice a gentleman of great judgement and practice in physic to be of special regard for many purpose this gum be black and brittle much like in show to common pitch the virtue of Colliman or Carriman if you put a little of it upon burn coal it fill all the room with a most sweet and pleasant savour he further report of it that certain if you hold your head over the fume thereof three or four time a day it cure the giddiness of the head and be also a most excellent comfort and remedy for a cold moist and rheumatic brain it be also good against the resolution or as the common sort call it the dead palsy whereof the giddiness of the head be often a messenger and the fore-teller of that most pernicious grief it be also of great use for the pain that many woman have in the low part of their back which be very common to such as have have child for remedy whereof it be to be melt in a pewter vessel with a gentle fire then with a knife it must be spread light upon a piece of leather and lay warm to the place grieve until it come off of itself this plaster be also very good for ache and do great comfort and strengthen the sinew thus much have master Cary write and report of it and the Colliman help the gout have prove by his own experience this gum be also approve to be a excellent remedy against the gout and of singular virtue in the cure of wound the Barratta be a most sovereign balsamum far excel all other yet know which by Barratta a rare the same gentleman experience be of admirable operation in the cure of green wound and be burn upon coal be of a sweet and odoriferous savour there be many other sweet gum of great use for perfume whereo^ one do make a perfume like sweet Margerum a very rare perfume much like unto the scent of sweet Margerum very pleasant and delectable for physic there be also many excellent drug namely spikenard cassia fistula Sene and drug and simple for physic the earth yield bolearmoniack and Terra-Lemnia all which be know unto we there be other drug and simple also of strange and rare virtue in these part unknown of which sort there be a little green apple by the indian call in their language the sleep apple which in operation be so violent that one little bit thereof do cause a man to sleep to death a apple which provoke sleep to death the least drop of the juice of it will purge in vehement and excessive manner as dangerous be prove by my cousin unton fisher who first find it for bite a little of it for a taste and find it to burn his mouth in some extremity do sudden spit it out again but some small quantity of the juice against his will go down into his stomach which for two or three day space do provoke in he a extraordinary sleepiness and purge he with sixty seat this apple for the purge virtue in so small a quantity be like to be of good price and great estimation in the practice of physic for the learned physician do well know how to correct the sleep quality thereof wherein the danger rest there be a berry in those part very excellent against the bloudie-fluxe by the indian it be call Kellette the juice of the leaf call a berry cure the bloody flux a leaf cure the wound of the poison arrow a leaf cure the headache a wood that make fish drink Vppee cure the wound of the poison arrow the juice of the leaf call be good against the headache many other drug and simple be there find of singular property both in physic and chirurgery which if they shall be several describe according to their value and worthiness will contain a large volume moreover the tree wherewith they take their fish be not a little to be esteem but chief the great goodness of God therein be high to be praise and admire who among so many admirable thing by he create and plant in those part have vouchsafe to bestow upon those barbarous people so great a benefit and natural help for the present get of their food and sustenance these tree be common grow near unto the place of their habitation for their present use for when at any time they go to fish they take three or four little stick of this tree and bruise they upon a stone and then go into certain small creek by the sea-shoare which at a high water be usual full of very good fish of diverse kind which come in with the tide and there they wade up and down the water and between their hand rub those small bruise stick therein which be of such virtue that they will cause the fish to turn up their belly and lie still above the water for a certain time in which space they present take as many as they please and lade they into their canoe and so with little labour return home sufficient provide there be also a red speckled wood in that country call which be worth thirty or forty pound a tun it be excellent for joiners work as chair stonles bedsteads press cupboard and for wainscot there be diverse kind of stone of great use and good price as jasper Porphyry and the spleene-sione there be yet another profitable commodity to be reap in Guiana and that be by tobacco which albeit some dislike yet the generality of man in this kingdom do with great affection tobacco entertain it it be not only in request in this our country of England but also in Ireland the netherlands in all the easterly country and Germany and most of all among the turk and in Barbary the price it hold be great the benefit our merchant gain thereby is-infinite and the king rend for the custom thereof be not a little the tobacco that be bring into this kingdom in the year of our lord 1610. be at the least worth 60. thousand pound and since 60000. worth of tobacco in a year that time the store that yearly have come in be little less it be plant gather season and make up fit for the merchant in short time and with easy labour but when we first arrive in those part we altogether want the true skill and knowledge how to order it which now of late we happy have learn of the spaniard themselves whereby I dare presume to say and hope to prove within few month as other also of sound judgement and great experience do hold opinion that only this commodity tobacco so much seek after and desire will bring as great a benefit and profit to the undertaker as ever the spaniard gain by the best and rich silver i in all their indies consider the charge of both the thing which the indian desire from we by way of trade in exchange for the above name the comodity most esteem by the indian commodity whereby we hold society and commerce with they be axe hatchet billhooke knife all kind of edge-tool nail great fishhook harping-iron jew trumpet looking-glass blue and white bead crystal bead hat pin needle salt shirt band linen and woollen clothes sword musket caleever powder and shoot but of these last mention we be very spare and part not with many unless upon great occasion by way of gift to special person when the rain cease which be in july I begin to travel abroad in search of those golden mountain promise unto we before the begin of our voyage by one that undertake leaden mind mind nothing but golden mine to guide we to they which fill my company so full of vain expectation and golden hope that their insatiable and covetous mind be whole set thereon can not be satisfy with any thing but only Gold our guide that vain make those great promise be come unto the wish place to make performance be then possess with a shameless spirit of ignorance for he know little and can perform nothing what other intelligence of mine already find I have from other man in England and from the master of my ship who have be heretofore in those part I find they by experience false and nothing true concern mine that be in England report unto i our greedy desire of gold be thus make frustrate diverse unconstant person of my unruly disorder by mutiny company begin to murmur to be discontent to kindle discord and dissension and to stir up mutiny even almost to the confusion and ruin of we all and be upon the point to shake off all obedience to their commander to abandon patience peace and unity and wilful to break out into all mischief and wretched disorder only because they be deceive of their golden hope and expectation but with good word and comfortable persuasion I pacify they for the time and make they acquaint with my better hope conceive of the commodity above mention I persuade they in general from idleness to travel abroad to search and seek out among the indian what other novelty they can though gold be want good to be do somewhat to prevent the devil whereby we may hereafter benefit ourselves and still I employ they some one way and some another to occupy their mind by do something the better to prevent dissension which common be breed of idleness the slothful mother of all filthy as I daily converse among the indian it chance one day that one of they present i with a half moon of metal which hold somewhat more than a three part gold the rest copper another also give i a little image of the same metal and of another I buy a plate the high countroy of Guiana abound with image of Gold of the same which he call a spread eagle for a axe all which thing they assure i be make in the high country of Guiana which they say do abound with image of gold by they call carrecoory these thing I show to my company to settle their trouble mind which give much contentment to the great part of they and satisfy we all that there be gold in Guiana short after that my indian Anthony Canabre bring i a piece of a rock the rock of the pure white sparre be mine of gold or silver of white sparre whereof the high country be full and if the white Sparres of this kind which be the pure white of all other for every sort of i have a sparre and for the most part white be in a main rock they be certain mine of gold or silver or of both I make trial of a piece of sparre which the same indian discover unto i and I find that it hold both gold and silver which although it be in small quantity give i satisfction that there be rich mine in the country to be find but the best lie deep in the earth and we have not time nor power to make search for they I travel up the river of Wiapoco to view the overfals but the water be high and strong I can not pass they in August when they be fall with some labour they may be pass many over-fal^ in Wiapoco this river have very many over-falls lie one a good distance beyond another even to the head thereof above some of the first fall there dwell a indian call comarian who be a old man of a free disposition by he I learn that a certain distance above the first fall the river Arwy fall into Wiapoco moreover that certain day journey beyond he towards the high land upon the border of Wiapoco there be a nation of charibe have great ear of a extraordinary bigness hard to be believe who he call Marashewaccas among these people as comarian report there be a idol of stone which they worship as their god they have place it in a house make of purpose for the great honour of it which they keep very people have great ear perhaps these ear be make large by art as diverse east indian use the proportion of their idol clean and handsome this idol be fashion like a man sit upon his heel hold open his knee and rest his elbow upon they hold up his hand with the palm forward look upward and gape with his mouth wide open the meaning of this proportion he can dot declare although he have be many time among they and have often see it what other nation be beyond these he do not know have never travel so far but he say they be charibe and also enemy unto they it seem there be many nation of those great ear people for in the river of Marrawini I hear also the like who dwell far up be the uttermost point of land to the northward in the bay of Wiapoco I find the soil of it most excellent for tobacco Maix cotton-tree annoto-tree vine and for any other thing that shall be plant company and of the indian also I take possession of the land by turf and twig in the behalf of our sovereign lord king james I take the say possession of a part in name of the whole continent of Guiana lie betwixt the river of amazon and Orenoque not be actual possess and inhabit by any other christian prince or state wherewith the indian seem to be well content and please in like manner my brother captain Michael Harecourt and captain Harvey who I leave as his associate and he esteem as a inward friend in a notable journey which to their great honour they perform to discover the river of Arrawary and the country border upon it near adjoin to the river of amazon do take the like possession of the land there to his majesty use the like possession take at Arrawary the danger and great difficulty which they in that attempt encounter be memorable and such as hardly any of our nation in such small canoe be only somewhat long but not so broad as our Thames wherry and flat-bottomed ever overcome the like first the number of their own attendant beside themselves be only one man and a boy their troop of indian sixty person their journey by sea unto the river of Arrawary be near one hundred league wherein by the way they meet with many dreadful plunge by reason of a high go sea which break upon the flat and shoald especial at the next great cape to the north of Arraway which in respect of the danger they pass there they name point perilous point Perilow then their discovery up the river be fifty league more where they find a nation of indian which never have see white man or christian before and can not be draw to any familiar commerce or conversation no not so much as with our indian because they be stranger to they and of another nation the discovery of this river be of great importance and special note afford a entrance more behooveful for the search and discovery of the inland part of Guiana than any other river yet know upon the coast for trend westward up into the land it discover all the country and nation to the southward of arricary Cooshebery Morrownia and norrack which I have mention before many week they spend in this adventure still take up their lodging in the wood at night provision of meat they want not for fish be ever plenty and at hand and the wood yield either dear tiger or fowl their great want be of bread and drink a great argument of plenty in the country which only defect do hinder at that time the accomplishment of that discovery for when the indian perceive their bread to be near spend and their drink to be corrupt they can not be persuade to proceed have no mean to supply their want among the arrawary the indian of that river who will not free trade with they upon this first acquaintance but always stand upon their guard on the other side of the river where they inhabit yet desire to obtain some of our english commodity and make trial of our indian friendship afford some small trade for their present relief during their abode in that river so that of force they be constrain to break off their discovery and hasten homeward but here their danger end not for as they return arrive at certain land call carripoory and pass between they and the main land much against the will of all the indian who know the danger of the place and more respect their safety than their own be themselves all expert swimmer will have dissuade they from that hazard but they be ignorant of the peril will needs pass on and at the last meet with such a boor as the seaman a dangerous boor at carvipapoory term it and violent encounter of two tide come in which like two furious enrage ram or bull rush together and oft retire back to return again with great violence until the one by force have over-borne the other that if next under God the diligent care and pain of the indian have not preserve they they have be there destroy and swallow up by that merciless boor or breach of water which God be thank they escape and return home in safety Annoto and other commodity whatsoever which shall hereafter be either plant or grow within the say mountain if it be demand the indian most glad receive the possession upon these condition and for himself and his posterity do promise to be true subject unto the king majesty his heir and successor and to pay the duty impose upon they and so that business be finish I return again to Wiapoco now most worthy prince there come unto my knowledge a inconvenience happen by the careless negligence of the master of my ship who have the charge of provide and lay in the only cause of loss by the voyage the provision and victual for the voyage which be the cause that I gain no present profit by it but leave off all my discovery in the first beginning I have a purpose at that time to perform a business which may have prove profitable and honourable unto we if I have be able to have stay the time but it be not my chance to be so fortunate for the master his mate and the steward of my ship come unto i and tell i plain that if I make any long abode in that country I will never in those ship return into England or if I do adventure it myself and all my company will starve at sea for want of beer cider and water for all my cask be spoil because it be not iron-bound the wooden hoop fly off by reason of the heat of the climate and our beer and cider whereof we have good store do leak about the ship that we can hardly save sufficient to relieve we if we make a long stay upon the coast which be the master fault have have a special charge to be careful of that only point by this default I be constrain to make a virtue of necessity and prepare myself for England and leave my former purpose to be accomplish hereafter which shall be do God aid i in time convenient then dispose of my company I appoint my brother captain Michael Harecourt to cap. Michael Harecourt leave commander of the company remain in the country as chief commander in my absence and to continue the possession on the king behalf I give he direction to travel abroad as occasion serve to discover the country to spend sometime at Cooshebery and sometime also in other place but to make his chief residence at Wiapoco the only rendezvouz for ship that trade upon that coast and there to plant good store of Maix for our relief of bread and drink which be the chief thing to be respect in those part for other victual we need not take much care be always easy provide he perform his charge with great reputation discover many goodly province possession continue 3. year and spacious country and worthy continue the possession full three year complete I leave with he for his assistance captain Harvey who have noble vow his time and fortune to be employ in the prosecution of this honourable action for his lieutenant I appoint twenty man leave with captain harcourt at Wiapoco master Edward gifford a valiant and worthy gentleman and I leave also with he of gentleman and other about twenty more with all such necessary as I can spare and think convenient for they and so commend they to God the eighteen day of August I depart from Wiapoco and the day follow arrive at Caiane at my come to Caiane my pinnace receive a leak which will have prove dangerous if we have be far at sea whereby enforce to attend the stop thereof and new trim the pinnace receive a leak at Caiane of the pinnace and unwilling to be idle in the mean space do nothing I leave my ship there to repair their defect and in my shipboate depart thence the twenty three of August take with i captain Fisher who have ever be since we first creep into the world my chief companion both in arm and travel I take also with i his brother Unton Fisher master cradle the master mate of my ship and about six more I follow the coast to r. whereof for the strangeness of they I can forbear to add a word or two these plant or little tree have assure the sense of feeling as plain appear by touch tree which have the sense of feeling these grow both in the east indies and in guinne see 10. Gom^^ 1. l. 9 they for if you do but touch a leaf of the tree with your finger that leaf will present shrink and close up itself and hang down as if it be dead and if you do cut off a leaf with a pair of cizzer than all the other leave grow upon the same tree will instant shrink and close up themselves and hang down as if they be dead and wither and within half a quarter of a hour will by degree open themselves again and flourish as before and as often as you do either touch or cut off any of they they will do the like which do evident show a restriction of the spirit invincible argue a sense howsoever this may seem strange and incredible to your highness and to they that have not see it yet forasmuch as Scaliger and Bartas make mention of the like I dare be bold to affirm it upon my credit have Scaliger Exercit. 181. sect. 28. come thither I be grievous vex with a extreme cough which I much fear will turn i to great harm but by bathe in the bath and drink of the water I be speedy cure and ever since that time I have find hand with a man hand burn with gunpowder and by the bath cure in 24. hour gunpowder and be in doubt thereby to loose the use of one or two of his finger which be shrink up with the fire but he go present to the bath and wash and bathe his hand a good space therein which soople his finger in such manner that with great ease he can stir and stretch they out and the fire be so wash out of his hand that within the space of twenty four hour by twice or thrice wash and bathe it the soreness thereof be cure only the eyesore for the time remain furthermore two or three other of my company have swell in the leg cure in a day swell in their leg be by the bath cure in a day hence we depart the sixteen day of October in the afternoon and leave the land of they depart from meve saint Christopher those that die thirty there die but six whereof one be drown another be a old man of threescore year of age and another take his death by his own disorder the rest die of sickness as please God the say not too dismal and fatal for our relation chap. 18 a description and discovery of the river of amazon by william Davies barber surgeon of London the river of the amazon lie in the high part of the west indies beyond the distant from England 1600. league this be a part of a book ^et forth by the say Davies of his miserable captivity equinoctial line to fall with this river forty league from land you shall have 8. 6. and 7. fathom water and you shall see the sea change to a ruddy colour the water shall grow fresh by these sign you may run bold in your course and come near the river mouth the depth of your water shall increase than you shall make discovery of the tree before the land by reason the land be very low and not high in one place then another three foot be at a spring tide almost all overflow God know how many hundred league it flow much water there with a very forcible tide in this river I continue ten week see the fashion of the people and country there this country be altogether full of wood with all sort of wild beast as lion bear wolf leopard baboon strange boor ape monkey Martin marmoset with diverse other strange beast also these wood be full of wild-fowl of all sort and parrot more plentiful than pigeon in England and as good meat for I have often eat of they also this country be very full of river have a king over every river in this place be continual tempest as lightning thunder and rain and so extreme that it continue most common sixteen or eighteen hour in four and twenty there be many stand water in this country which be full of aligator Guianes with many other several water serpent and great store of fresh fish of strange fashion this country be full of Muskitas which be a small fly which much offend a stranger come new into the country the manner fashion and nature of the people be this they be altogether naked both man and woman have not so much as one thread about they to cover any part of their nakedness the man take a round cane as big as a penny candle and two inch in length through the which he pull the foreskin of his yard tie the skin with a piece of the rind of a tree about the bigness of a small packthread then make of it fast about his middle he continue thus till he have occasion to use he in each ear he wear a reed or cane which he bore through it about the bigness of a swan quill and in length half a inch and the like through the midst of the low lip also at the bridge of the nose he hang in a reed a small glisse beade or button which hang direct afore his mouth fly too and fro still as he speak wherein he take great pride and pleasure he wear his hair long be round below to the neither part of his ear and cut short or rather as I judge pluck bald on the clown like a ^rier but their woman use no fashion at all to set forth themselves but stark naked as they be bear with hair long of their head also their breast hang very low by reason they be never lace or brace up they do use to anoint their body both man and woman with a kind of red earth because the muskita or fly shall not offend they these people be very ingenious crafty and treacherous very light of foot and good boweman who like I have never see for they do ordinary kill their own food as beast fowl and fish the manner of their bow and arrow be this the bow be about two yard in length the arrow seven foot his bow be make of brasill-wood very curious his string of the rind of a tree lie close to the Bo^ without any bent his arrow make of reed and the head of it be a fish bone (@) a beast in this manner stand behind a tree he take his mark at the beast and woe (...) (@) he follow he like a bloodhound till he fall oftentimes second his shoot then for any fowl be he never so little he never miss he as for the first he walk by the water side and when he have spy a fish in the water he present strike he with his arrow and sudden throw down his bow he leap into the water swim to his arrow which he draw aland with the fish fasten to it then have each kill his own food as well flesh and foul as fish they meet together to the number of fifty or sixty in a company then make a fire after this fashion they take two stick of wood rub one hard against another till such time as they be fire then make of a great fire every man be his own cook to broil that which he have get and thus they feed without bread or salt or any kind of drink but water and tobacco neither do they know what it mean in these country we can find neither gold nor silver oar but great store of hen for I have buy a couple for a jew harp when they will refuse ten shilling in money this country be full of delicious fruit as pine plantine guave and potato rootes of which fruit and root I will have buy a man burden for a glass button or bead. the manner of their lodging be this they have a kind of net make of the rind of a tree which they call Haemac be three fathom in length and two in breadth and gather at both end at length then fasten either end to a tree to the full length about a yard and half from the ground when he have desire to sleep he creep unto it the king of every river be know by this manner he wear upon his head a crown of parrot feather of several colour have either about his middle or about his neck a chain of lion tooth or claw or of some other strange beast have a wooden sword in his hand and hereby be he know to be the king oftentimes one king war against another in their canowes which be boat cut out of a whole tree sometime take one another the conqueror eat the captive by this time ten week be spend and be homeward bind but not the same way that we come for we sail unto the river before the wind because it blow there continual one way which force all ship that come thither to return by a contrary way the end of the six book voyage to and about the southern America with many marine observation and discourse of those sea and land by englishman and other the seven book reader I here present thou the exact treatise of brasil of Dartmouth in a u^yage outward bind for brasil an. 1601. who sell the same to master Hacket for twenty shilling by who procurement it be translate out of Portugal into english which translation I Portugal which have long live there @. i. of the beginning and original of the indian of brasil and of their custom religion and ceremony it seem that this people have no knowledge of the beginning and creation of the world but of the deluge it seem they their opinion of a flood have some notice but as they have no write nor character such notice be obscure and confuse for they say that the water drown all man and that one only escape upon a with a sister of his that be with child and that from these two they have their beginning and from thence begin their multiply and increase of the knowledge that they have or the creator and of the soul paradise devil this people have not any knowledge of their creator no^ of any thing of heaven nor if there be any pain nor glory after this life therefore they have no oderation nor ceremony nor divine worship but they know that they have soul and that they die not and they say that the soul be convert into devil and that after their death they go to certain field where be many fig tree along by a fair river and all together do nothing but dance this be the cause why they be g^tatly afraid of the devil who they call Curupira Taguain Pigtangna A^hanga and their fear of he be so great that only with the imagination of he they die as many time already it have happen they worship it not not any other creature neither have they idol of any sort only some old man do say that in some way they have certain post where they offer he some thing for the fear they have of they and because they will not die sometime the devil appear unto they though very seldom and among they devil fear be few possess th^y use some witchcraft and there be some witch not because they believe in they or do worship they but only they give themselves to the Chupar in their sickness seem to they that they receive their health but not because they do think they have any divinity and they do it rather to receive health then for any other respect there arise sometime among they some witch who they call Caraiba and most common it be some indian of a bad life this do some witchcraft and strange thing to nature as to show that he raise some to life that juggle make himself dead and with these and other l^ke thing he carry all the country after he deceive and say to they that they shall not cultivate nor plant their pulse and their provision neither dig nor labour etc. for with his come the time be come that the mattock themselves shall dig of their own accord and the beast go to the field and bring the provision and with these falsehood he lead they so delude and enchant that not look to their life and to get their food they die for hunger and these company be diminish by litand little till the Caraiba remain alone or be murder by they they have no proper name to express God but they say the tupan be the thunder and lightning no proper name of God and that this be he that give they the mattock and the food and because they have no other name more natural and proper they call God Tupan there be marriage among they but there be a great doubt whether they be true as well because of the marriage they give no dowry to their daughter or to the but they serve their mother in law they have many wife as for the easy forsake they for whatsoever quarrel anger or any other disgrace happen among they but either true or not among they they be make in this sort no young man do use to marry before he have take a emenie and he continue a virgin till he take and slay he hold first his feast for the space of two or three year the woman in like sort do not marry nor know man till she have her term after the which they make her great feast at the time of the delivery of the woman they make great drink and the feast be end the marriage remain perfect give a net clean wash and after they be say the father take a wedge of stone and do cut upon a post or stake than they say he tail do cut the tail from the grandchild and therefore they be bear without they and after they be marry they begin to drink for until then their father do not suffer they teach they that they shall drink heedful and shall be considerate and wise in their drink speak that the wine may do they no hurt and that they shall not speak bad thing and then with a vessel the old ancient man do give he the first wine and hold his head with their hand that he may not vomit for if he do vomit they hold to themselves that he will not be valiant this people eat at all time by night and by day and every hour and moment and when of the manner th^y keep in their eat and drink they have any meat they keep it no long time for they have no providence for the future but present they eat all that they have and divide it among their friend in sort that of one fish that they have they divide it to all and they hold for a great honour and gallantry to be liberal and thereby they get great fame and honour and they hold for the great injury that liberality and opinion of niggardi^e they can do they to hold they for niggard or call they so and when they have nothing to eat they be very patient in hunger and thirst they have no flesh or fish day they eat all manner of flesh even of unclean creature as snake toad rat and such like worm they eat also all manner of fruit save some that be poisonous this sustenance be ordinary of that which the country yield without husbandry as wild fowl flesh and fruit their diet but they have a certain kind of food of a good substance and healthful and many other pulse whereof hereafter shall mention be make ordinary they drink not while they eat but after meat they drink water or wine which they make of many kind of fruit and root as hereafter shall be say of the which they drink without measure or order even till drink they fall down they have some particular day wherein they make great feast and all end in drink and they last two or three day in the which they eat not but only drink and there be man that feast empty a whole great vessel of wine that these drink may be more festival some go about sing from house to house call and invite all they find for to drink and be merry these dance last with music all the time of the drink in the which they sleep not but pass it all in drink and when they be drink they play many disorder and they break dance one another head and take other man wife etc. they give no thanks before nor after meat rudeness to God nor wash their hand before meat and after meat they wipe they at their hair on their body or a post they have no towel nor table they eat fit or lie in their net or cower on the ground they eat their meat throw it with their hand into the mouth and I omit many other particularity that they have in their eat and drink because these be the principal all this people have for their bed certain net make of Cotten wool and they sleep in of the manner that they have in their sleep they hang in the air these they make some wrought other of sundry colour and as they remain in the air and have no other cover or clothes all way in summer and winter they have fire under they they rise not very early and go to bed by time and in the morning there be one chief man in their house * * one house contain many family that lie in his net do preach unto they for the space of a hour how they be to go to labour as their forefather do and he appoint they the time tell they what they be to do and after he be up continue his preach run through the town they take this custom from a bird which be like a hawk which sing in the morning and they call it the king and lord of the other bird and they say that even as that bird do sing in the morning to be hear of the rest so the principal shall make those preach and speech to be hear of they all of they go naked as well man as woman and have no kind of apparnll and be nothing nakedness ashamed rather it seem that they be in the state of innocence touch this behalf by the great honesty and modesty they do keep among themselves and when any man speak modesty paint with a woman he turn his back to she but to make themselves gallant they use diverse invention paint their body with the juice of a certain fruit wherewith they remain black make in their body many white stroke after the fashion of round hose and other kind of gallantry garment they enplume themselves also make diadem and bracelet and other very fine invention they esteem very much all manner of fine feather they let no hair grow in the part of their body but they pull they out only the head except which they cut in many fashion for some wear they long with a half moon shave before and they say they take neatness this use from saint Thomas and it seem that they have some notice of he though confuse other make certain kind of crown and circle that they seem friar the woman all do wear long hair and ordinary black and the hair of the one and of the other be smooth when they be angry they let their hair grow long and the woman when they mourn do mourn cut their hair and also when their husband go a far journey in this they show their love and loyalty to they the vanity they have in their poll be so much that by the head the nation be know now already some do wear apparel as well man as woman but they esteem it so little apparel that they wear it rather for fashion then for honesty sake and because they be command to wear it as it be well see by some that sometime come abroad with certain garment no further than the navel without any other thing and other only with a cap on their head and leave the other garment at home the woman make great account of lace and comb these indian do use certain cottage or house of timber cover with palm tree leave of their house and be in length some of two hundred and three hundred span and they have two or three door very little and low they show their valour in seek timber and very great post and of great continnance and there be house that have fifty sixty or seventy room of twenty or five and twenty quarter long and as many quarter long and as many in breadth in this house dwell one principal man or more who all the rest do obey and ordinary they be kinfman in every room of these dwell a household with their child and family without any repartition between the one and the other and to enter in one of these house be to enter into a labyrinth for every room have his fire and their net hang and their ^stuffe so that come in all that they have be in sight and some house have two hundred person and more the woman when they be bring to bed they be deliver on the ground do not childbirth take up the child but the father take it up or some other person who they take for their gossip and in friendship they be as the gossip among the christian the father do cut the navel string with his tooth or with two stone knock the one with the other and then they set themselves to fast until the navel string fall off which be ordinary to the eight day and till it do fall they leave not their fast when it fall if it be a man child he make it a bow with arrow and tie it at the end of the net and at the other end many handful of herb which be the enemy which his son shall kill and eat these ceremony be end they make drink where with they all be merry the woman when they be deliver do present go and wash themselves in the river and they give the child suck ordinary a year and a half not give it any other thing to eat they love their child extraordinary and bear they in certain piece of net which they call Tupiya and carry love and e^^cation of child they to their plow and to all kind of labour on their back through cold and heat and they carry they like the g^p^ies straddle about their hip they give they no manner of correction that their child may not cry they have many southsaying for they put cotton-clothe upon their head bird teather and stick they lay they one the palm of their hand and rock they by they that they may grow they esteem more to do good to their child then to themselves and now they esteem and love the father very much because they friar and jesuire pain with indian child bring they up they teach they to read write and cipher and sing and to play on a instrument a thing which they do much esteem when any guest do come to the house the honour and entertainment they make he be to of the custom they have in harbour or entertain their guest bewail he now the guest be come into the house they set he in the net and after he be set without speak any word to he the wife and the daughter and the other friend do sit they down round about he with their hair loose touch with the hand the party they all begin to weep with a high voice and great abundance of tear and there they tell in a versify prose all thing that have happen since they see one another to that hour and many other which they invent and the trouble that the guest have suffer in his journey and all thing else that may provoke pity and tear the guest all this time speak not one word but after they have bewail he a good while thy wipe the tear and remain so quiet so modest so pleasant and merry that it seem they never weep and then they salute one another and give their ereiupe or welcome and they bring he meat etc. and after these ceremony end the guest tell wherefore he come the man likewise bewail one another but it be in some weighty matter as death misfortune in war etc. they hold it for a great courtesy to entertain all man and to give they all thing necessary for their sustenance and some gift as bow arrow bird feather and other thing according to their poverty without any kind of reward these gentile do accustom to drink the smoke of petigma by another name the holy herb of the custom they have of drink of smoke this they dry and make of a palmtree leaf a coffin like the joint of a cane and fill with this herb they fire it at the small end put the big in their mouth and so they suck or drink that smoke and they hold it for a great dainty and favour and lie in their net they spend part of the day and of the night to some it do much hurt and make they dizzy and drink to other it do much good and make they void a great deal of fiegme at the mouth the woman also do drink it but they be such as be old and sickly for it be very medicinable unto they especial for the cough the headache and the disease of the stomach and hence come a great many of the portugal to drink it and have take it for a vice or for idleness imitate the indian to spend day and night about it this nation have no money where with to satisfy the service that be do to they but they of the manner of payment and husbandry live with barter one thing for another and principal in change of wine they do all that they will and so when they have any business they make wine and advise the neighbour and assemble all the town they desire they to help they in their husbandry which they do with a good will and labour till ten of the clock they return home again to drink their wine and if that day their tillage be not end they make other wine and so go another day till ten of the clock to make a end of their business and in this sort do the wise white man or portugal use that know the use and fashion of the indian and how much they do for wine they make wine for they and call they to their husbandry and to their sugarcane and with this they pay they they use also ordinary to change some thing for white bead which be make of wilkes and in change of some nosegay they give even their wife and this be the ransom wherewith they use ordinary that be the white man for to buy of they the slave as well man as woman that they have for to eat these indian use ordinary chief in their feast collar which they make of wilkes diadem of feather and certain brooch that be stone which they put in their low of their jewel and brooch lip some green white some blue and very fine and be like emerald or crystal they be round and some of they so long that they reach to their breast and it be ordinary among the filthy fine great and principal man to have they of a span or more in length they use also white bracelet of the same wilkes and they put in their ear certain white stone of a span long and more and these and other like be the ornament wherewith they adorn themselves in their feast whether they be of slaughter of the enemy or of wine and these be the riches that they esteem above all that they possess these indian do use to entreat their wife well they never strike they neither quarrel of the usage of their wife and how they man they with they except in the time of their drink for then ordinary they revenge themselves of they give for a excuse afterward it be the wine they have drink and then they be friend as before and the hatred between they last not long they go always together and when they go abroad the woman come behind and the man before that if any ambush be lay the wife may not fall into it and may have time to fly while the husband fight with his adversary etc. but at their return home from their field or from any other place the wife come before and the husband behind that if any mischance shall happen the wife may fly home and the husband fight with the enemy or any other thing but in a safe country and within the town the wife always go before and the husband behind for they be very jealous and will have always their wife in sight jealousy of their dance and their song though they be melancholic they have their game especial the child very diverse and pleasant in the which they counterfeit many kind of bird and with so great feast and order as may be and the child be joyful and give to play and they play with such quietness and friendship that among they be no bad name hear or any scurrility or call any nickname one to another father or mother and seldom do they disagree when they play nor disorder themselves for any thing and very seldom do they strike or fight one with another the father do teach they from their cradle to dance and sing and their dance be not sundry change but a continual stamp with the foot stand still or go round about or stir their body or their head and they do it all by such compass and pleasantness as can be desire at the sound of a timbrel make after the fashion of those which the child use in instrument Spain with many small stone within or certain seed whereof they make also very good bead and so they sing dance altogether for they do not one thing without the other in such compass and order that sometime a 100 man dance and sing together in a row one behind the other do end all at one stroke as if they be altogether in one place the singer aswell man as woman be much esteem among they in so much that if they take a enemy a good singer and a inventer of verse they therefore spare his life and do not eat he nor his child the woman do dance together with the man and make many gambol and gesture with woman dance their arm and body especial when they dance alone they keep among themselves difference of voice in their consort and ordinary the woman do sing the treble counter and tenour they be very wicked especial in weep for the dead for when any one die the kindred of their burial do cast themselves upon he in the net and so sudden that sometime they choke he before he die seem to they he be dead and those that can cast themselves with the coarse in the net do cast themselves on the ground with such fall and knock that it seem lamentation to be lament a miracle they do not end their life with the dead and of these fall and mourn they remain so feeble that sometime they die when they mourn they speak many pitiful and dolorous word and if he die at evening all night long they weep with a high voice that it be a wonder they be not weary for these mourn they call the neighbour and kinsman and if he be one of the principal all the town do meet to mourn and in this they have also their point of honour and they curse with plague those which weep not say that they shall not be mourn for after he be dead they wash he and paint he very brave as they paint their enemy and after this they cover he with Cotton yarn that nothing be see of he and put a cover over his face and sit they put he in a great tinnage or vessel that they have under the earth for that purpose and do cover it in such manner that no earth may come to he and the vessel they cover with earth make he a house where every day they carry he meat for they say that when he be weary with dance he come thither to eat and so they go for a certain time to bewail he every day all his kindred with he they bury all his jewel or brooch that none may see they and grieve thereat but if the dead have any piece as a sword etc. that have be give he it return to he that give it and he take it again wheresoever he find it therefore they say that when one die he lose all the right of that which be give he after the coarse be bury the kinsman be in continual weep night and day the one beginning as the other end they eat not but by night they hang their net near to the roof and the woman after twenty day do cut their hair and this lament last a whole moon the which be end they make great wine or drink to put away their mourn the man do cut their hair and the woman do paint themselves with black and these ceremony and other be end they begin to communicate the one with the other aswell the man as the woman after their companion be dead some never do marry again nor enter into the feast of wine neither paint themselves with black but be very seldom among they because they be much give to woman and can live without they before they have any knowledge of the portugal they use tool and instrument of stone of the instrument they do use bone wood cane and tooth of beast etc. and with these they hew down great wood with wedge of stone help themselves with fire and they dig also the ground with certain sharp stake and they make their brooch bead of wilkes Bowes and arrow as well as now have instrument of iron but they spend a long time in make of whatsoever thing wherefore they esteem the iron very much for the facility or ease which they find in make their thing with it and this be the reason wherefore they be glad of commerce with the portugal or white man the weapon of this people ordinary be Bowes and arrow and they boast themselves of of the weapon they do use they and they make they of very good wood and very fair interlay with palmtree of sundry colour they die their string green or red and they make their arrow very fair seek for they the fair feather they can find they make these arrow of sundry cane and fasten in their point the tooth of beast or certain very hard rush or sharp stick with many snagge and many time they empoison they with herb these arrow to one sight seem a thing of mockery but be very cruel weapon and pierce quilt breastplate or curate and strike in a stick they cleave it asunder and sometime happen to go through a man cruel arrow and stick on the ground they do exercise themselves in these weapon very young and be great archer and so certain that no bird can escape they be it never so little or any vermin cunning archer of the wood and there be no more but if they will shoot a arrow through the eye of a bird or a man or hit any other thing be it never so small they do it with great facility and with their own safety and for this they be great fear they be stout also and fierce and dreadful to other they be as vermin of the wood for they go a hunt into the country naked and barefoot without any fear they have a marvelous sight for at a league off they see any thing and their Arts. in the same manner they hear they guess very right rule themselves by the sun they go to all part they list 200. or 300. league through thick wood and miss not one ^ot they travel quick sight much and always run a gallop especial with some charge no horse be able to hold out with they they be great fisher and swimmer they fear no sea nor wave continue a great traveller and swift day and a night swim and the same they do row and sometime without meat they use also for weapon sword of wood and interlay the end of they with palmtree of sundry colour and set plume on they of diverse colour chief in their feast and slaughter and sword these sword be very cruel for they make no wound but bruise and break a man head without have any remedy of cure @. 2 of their manner of kill and eat of humane flesh and of their create gentleman of all the honour and pleasure of this life none be so great for this people as to kill and get a name on the head of their adversary neither be there among they any feast comparable to those which they make at the death of those which they kill with great ceremony which they do in this manner those which be take in the war be appoint to die come present from thence with a token which be a small cord about his neck and if he be a man that may runnne away he have one hand tie to his neck under his chin and before they come to the town that be by the way they paint their eyelid kickshaw and their beard poll they after fashion and enplume they with yellow feather so well place that you can see no hair which make they so gallant as the spaniard in their rich apparel and so they go share their victory whereby soever they pass when they come to their own country the woman come out to receive they shout altogether and strike themselves on the mouth which be a common entertainment among they without any other vexation or imprisonment except that they wear about the neck a round collar like a cord of a good bigness as hard as a stick in this collar they begin to weave a great many fathom of small cord as long as a woman hair fasten above with a certain knot and loose underneath and so it go from ear to ear behind the back horrible to look on and if it be on the frontier where he may run away they put he in stead of shackle below the knee a string of thread twist very hard which be too weak for any knife but that they have keeper that go not one moment from he whether he go about the house to the wood or by the field for he have liberty for all this and common the keeper be one that be give he for wife and also for to dress his meat with the which if his master do give he no meat as the custom be he take a bow gentle cruel keeper and arrow and shoot at the first hen he see or at a duck be it whosesoever and none do contradict he and so he wax fat neither break therefore his sleep his laughter or his pleasure as the rest and some be as content though they be to be eat that in no wise they will consent to be ransom for to serve for they say that it be a wretched thing to die and lie stink and eat with worm these woman be common faithful in their charge for they receive honour thereby and therefore many time they be young and daughter of the chief especial if their brother be to be the slaier for those which have not this interest many time affect they in such manner that not only they give they leave to run away but they also do go with they neither have the woman any other punishment if they be take again than a few stroke and sometime they be eat of those same to who they give life the time when he shall die be determine the woman begin to make vessel that be festival preparation and solemnity bowl tray and pot for the wine so great that every one will hold a pipe this be ready as well the principal as the rest do send their messenger to invite other from sundry place against such a moon about ten or twelve league compass or more for the which none do excuse himself the guest do come in mogote or troop with their wife and child and all of they do enter the town with dancer and all the time the people be a gather together there be wine for the guest for without it all the other entertainment be nothing worth the people be assemble the feast begin some day before according to the number and certain ceremony precede and every one last a day first they have for this certain coard of cotton-wool of a take pleasure it be to be believe that they be not make in a year these be always very safe keep and be carry to the place with great feast and great noise in certain tray where a master of these because of the fire catch hold of all that he can and catch they and they be many he miss few time at the three day they make a dance of man and woman all of they with pipe of cane and all of they at once do stamp on the ground now with one foot then with the other all together without miss a stroke and observe the same measure they play on their pipe and there be no other sing nor speak they be many and the cane some big and some small beside the resound black saint in the wood they make a hel-seeming harmony but they abide it as if it be the sweet music in the World and these be their feast beside other which they intermingle with many grace and soothsay on the four day they carry the captive enemy as soon as the day break to wash he at a river and they while the time that when they do alone without any other help so he will show courage and force in resist he first encounter and sometime he do it in such sort that the first stand aside as weary in wrestle another succeed he which with the collar he be more now with those two knot so big behind about his neck and therefore one of the verse of the song say we be those that make the neck of the bird to stretch although after continue with great ferventness all the day and night that the wine do their song etc. last for this be the proper feast of the slaughter in the drink of the wine be many particularity which last long and they make water at every stop and so they continue day and night they sing dance drink and speak tell in whoop through all the house of war and act that they do and as every one will be hear in his history every one do speak strive to be loud beside other noise without any intermission no not a quarter of a hour that morning in which they begin to drink they paint the captive by a particular way that they have for that design in this sort his face be clean and all the feather he have bring forth they anoint he with the milk of a certain tree that cleave very fast and they cast adorn of the captive upon it the powder of certain eggeshel of a certain wild bird and upon this they paint he with black very fair picture and all his body to the sole of his foot and stick he all with feather which they have already cut for that purpose and die read and that make he to seem half as big again and touch his face it make it seem as much great and the eye so much the small that he of the new knight that shall be and take the sword pass it many time between his leg put it now on the one side now on the other even in the same manner that the piper dog do pass between their leg and after take it by the midst with both hand he point as with a thrust to the eye of the man which be to die and this be do he turn the head of it upward in the same manner that he be to use it and put it in the hand of the slaughterer as apt and fit already with those blessing for to do his office they place themselves hallow the Sword somewhat to the left side in such sort that he may hit he with the edge of his sword in the nape of the neck for he strike at another place and their brutishness be so much that because they fear no other evil but that which be present they be as resolute as if it be nothing as well for to speak as for to try their courage for after they take their leave of life say in a good hour let i die see many be dead and that beside this his brethren and kinsman remain here to revenge they and with this the one make butchery rite he ready to discharge and the other to avoid his body which be all the honour of his death and they be so nimble in this that many time it be high day before they be able to kill they for when he see the weapon in the air sometime he draw his head aside sometime he decline his body and in this they be so doughty that if those that hold the point of the coard do gird he hard as they do when the slaughterer be slow or weak he pull so hard that he bring they to he and make they to slacken in despite have one eye on they another on the sword without any stand still and as the killer may not deceive they with a offer and not strike under pain of receive a fillip they do foresee their stroke in such sort that come it never so low in a trise they stoop and lie so flat that it be a wonder to see and no less be the take of the sword hold the arm in such sort that do he no hurt they pull it down joint with themselves and they put it under the arm pull by the killer wherein if they do not help the other will dispatch he for they have in this actson so many sooth-saying that for to kill a child of five year old they go so prepare as for to kill some giant and with these help and encouragement so many time he strike till he hit and that be enough for assoon as he be down he give he so many blow till he batter his head though one man be see that have it so hard that they can never break it for as they go barehead they have blockhead they so hard that we in comparison of they be like a pompion and when they will injury any white man they call he soft-head if this which they kill fall on his back and not on his belly they hold it for a evil luck and prognostication that the killer shall die and although he fall upon his belly they have many ceremony which if they be not keep they hold that the killer can live and many of they be so painful that if any one do suffer their trouble for God sake they will be account meritorious as hereafter shall be say the poor wretch be dead they carry he to a bonfire that they have ready for the same and bring the body near the fire touch he with the hand flay off a skin somewhat thick than the rind of a onion till he remain clean and white than a scald Pig then it be deliver to the butcher which make a hole beneath the stomach according to their use whereby the child first do put in their hand and pull by the gut until the butcher cut where he list and that which remain in the hand of every one be his part and the rest be divide among the commons except some principal piece which for great honour be give to the guest that be the most principal which they do carry well r (...) i so that it may not corrupt and with they afterward in their country they make Knivet principal which comprehend some ten nation of indian these live on the sea coast and in a great part of the land all of one speech though they differ in some word this be that which the portugal do understand it be easy eloquent pleasant and copious the difficulty of it be in have many comparison but of the portugal almost all those that come from the kingdom and be seat here and do communicate with the indian do know it in a short time and the child of the portugal bear here do speak it better than the Portugal as well man as woman chief in the captainship of saint Vincent and with these ten nation of indian have the father communication because they know their language and they more tame and well incline these be and be the ancient friend of the portugal with who help and arm they conquer this country fight against their own kindred and diverse other nation very barbarous and those of this generation be so many that it seem a portugal use of savage impossible thing to extinguish they but the portugal have make such haste that they be almost dead and they use such mean that they the coast and fly the land inward some three hundred some four hundred the first of this language be call pitiguaras lord of Parayba thirty league from pernambuco pitiguaras and have the best Brasill wood and be great friend to the frenchman and do contract with they until now marry their daughter with they but now in the year 1584. day be all the year almost equal the country be some what melancholic overflow with many water as well of main river as from the sky in it be great store of rain chief in winter it be full of great many way wonderful greatness as beauty some be take of five and twenty or thirty foot long and a yard in compass it have a chain along the back of notable picture and very fair that begin at the head and end in the tail it have tooth like a dog and lay hold on a man cow stag or hog wind it with certain turn of her tail it swallow the say thing whole and after she have it so in her belly she let herself rot and the raven and crow do eat she all so that there remain nothing but the bone and afterward it breed new flesh again and renew as before it be the reason whereof be say the man of the country because while it putrefy it have the head in the mire and have life in the noddle they live again and because this be know already when they find they putrify they seek o^t the head and kill it the manner of their feed be to wait for their prey either beast or people lay along by the way and when it pass it wind itself about it and kill and eat it after they be full they sleep in such sort that sometime they cut two or three piece of their tail they not wake as have happen that after they have cut two piece of the tail of one of these the next day they find her dead with two wild boar in her belly and it be about twelve yard and a half long the snake keep always in the water it be yet great than the other abovesaid it be much paint and from his picture do the gentlies of
