Gabriel ARCHAR touch the voyage of the fleet of ship which arrive at Virginia without sir tho. gate and sir GEORGE Summers 1609. from Woolwich the fifteen of May 1609 seven sail weigh anchor and come to Plymouth the twenty day where sir George Somers with two small vessel consort with we here we take into the blessing be the ship wherein I go fix mare and two horse and the fleet lay in some necessary belong to the action in which business we spend time till the second of and then we set sail to sea but cross by south-west wind we put in to Faulemouth and there stay till the eight of june we then gate out our course be command to leave the canary one hundred league to the the appoint course eastward at least and to steer away direct for Virginia without touch at the west indies except the fleet shall chance to be separate than they be to repair to the bermuda there to stay seven day in expectation of the admiral and if they find he not then to take their course to Virginia now thus it happen about six day after we lose the sight of England one of sir George Somers the ship and chief man in the Fleet. Pinnasses leave our company and as I take it bear up for England the rest of the ship viz. the sea adventure admiral wherein be sir Thomas gate sir George summer and captain Newport the diamond vide-admiral wherein be captain Ratcliff and captain King the falcon rear-admiral in which be captain Martin and master Nellson the blessing wherein I and captain adam go the unity wherein captain wood and master Pett be the lion wherein captain webb remain and the swallow of sir George Somers in which captain moon and master summer go in the catch go one Matthew fitch master and in the boat of sir George Somers call the Virginia which be build in the north colony go one captain Davies and one master Davies these be the captatines and master of our Fleet. we run a southerly course fro^ the tropic of cancer where have the sun within six or seven degree right over our head in july we bear away west so that by the fervent heat and loom breeze sickness and mortality at Sea many of our man fall sick of the calenture and out of two ship be throw overboard thirty two person the vice-admiral be say to have the plague in she but in the blessing we have not any sick albeit we have twenty woman and child upon saint james day be about one hundred and fifty league distant from the west indies in cross the gulf of Bahoma there happen a most terrible and vehement storm which be a tail of the terrible tempest west indian horacano this tempest separate all our fleet one from another and it be so violent that man can scarce stand upon the deck neither can any man hear another speak be thus divide every man steer his own course and as it fall out about five or six day after the storm cease which endure forty four hour in extremity the lion first and after the falcon and the unity get sight of our ship and so we lay a way direct for Virginia find neither current nor wind opposite as some have report to the great charge of our counsel and adventurer the unity be sore distress note false rumour chargeable when she come up with we for of seventy land man she have not ten sound and all her sea man be down but only the master and his boy with one poor sailer but we relieve they and we four consort fall into the king river haply the eleven of August in the unity be bear two child at sea but both die be both boy arrival in Virginia when we come to james town we find a ship which have be there in the river a month before we come this be send out of England by our counsel leave and authority to fish for sturgeon and to go the ready way without trace through the torrid Zoan and she perform it her commander be captain argol a good mariner and a very civil gentleman and her master one Robert tindal captain argall the people of our colony be find all in health for the most part howbeit when captain argol come in they be in such distress for many be disperse in the savage town live upon their alm state of the colony for a ounce of copper a day and fourscore live twenty mile from the fort and feed upon nothing but oyster eight week space have no other allowance at all neither be the people of the country able to relieve they if they will whereupon captain Newport and other have be much to blame to inform idleness and other vice to blame also the counsel of such plenty of victual in this country by which mean they have be slack in this supply to give convenient content upon this you that be adventurer must pardon we if you find not return of commodity so ample as you may expect because the law of nature bid we seek sustenance first and then to labour to content you afterward but upon this point I shall be more large in my next letter after our four ship have be in harbour a few day come in the vice-admiral have cut her main most over board and have many of her man very sick and weak but she can tell no news of our governor some thing partly false rumour partly faction suggestion be here leave out and some three or four day after she come in the swallow with her main mast overboard also and have a shrewd leak neither do she see our admiral now do we all lament much the absence of our governor for contention begin to grow and faction and partake etc. insomuch as the precedent to strengthen his authority accord with the mariner and give not any due respect to many worthy gentleman that come in our ship whereupon they choose a new governor they general have also my consent choose master west my lord la war brother to be their governor or precedent in the absence of sir Thomas gate or if he miscarry by sea then Henee from the malcontent which have be in Virginia before enemy to the precedent raise now ill report at their come of he arise these stir and the follow misery in which this author with almost the whole colony perish to continue till we hear news from our counsel in England this choice of he they make not to disturb the old precedent during his time but as his authority expire then to take upon he the sole govenment with such assistant of the captain as discreet person as the colony afford perhaps you shall have it blazon a mutiny by such as retain old malice but master west master Percy and all the respect gentleman of worth in Virginia can and will testify otherwise upon their oath for the king patent we ratify but refuse to be govern by the precedent that now be after his time be expire and only subject ourselves to master west who we labour to have next precedent I can certify you of much more as yet until we grow to some certain stay in this our state but by the other ship you shall know more so with my hearty commendation I cease from james town this last of Angust 1609. chap. 5 a true reportory of the wrack and redemption of sir THOMAS gate knight upon and from the land of the be by ^^ts some hour with more violence than other at length do beat all light from heaven which like a hell of darkness turn black upon we so much the more full of horror as in such case horror and at sea more featefull as who be most arm and best prepare be not a little shake for sure noble lady as death come not so sudden nor apparent so he come not so elvish and painful to man especial even then in health and perfect habitude of body as at sea who come at no time so welcome but our frailty so weak be the hold of hope in miserable demonstration of danger it make guilty of many contrary change and conflict for indeed death be accompany at no time nor place with circumstance every way so uncapable of particularity of goodness and inward comfort as at Sea for it be most true there arise common no such unmerciful tempest compound of so many contrary and diverse nation but that it work upon the whole frame of the body and most loathsome affect all the power thereof and the manner of the sickness it lay upon the body be so unsufferable give not the mind any free and quiet time to use her judgement and empire which make the poet say and and tremente for four and twenty hour the storm in a restless tumult have blow so exceed as continence and increase we can not apprehend in our imagination any possibility of great violence yet do we still find it not only more terrible but more constant fury add to fury and one storm urge a second more outrageous than the former whether it so wrought upon our fear or indeed meet with new force sometime strike in our ship among woman and passenger not use to such hurly and discomfort make we look one upon the other with trouble heart and pant bosom our clamour drown in the wind and the wind in thunder prayer may well be in the heart and lip but drown in the outcry of the officer nothing hear that can give comfort nothing see that may encourage hope it be impossible for i have I the voice of Stentor and expression of as many tongue as his throat of voice to express the outcry and misery not languish but waste his spirit and be constant to his own principle but not prevail our sail wound up lie without their use and if at any time we bear but a hollocke or half forecourse to guide she before the sea six and sometime eight man be not enough to hold the whipstaffe in the steerage and the tiler below in the gunner room by devil etc. rather because they be so terrible to all that ever touch on they and such tempest thunder and other fearful object be see and hear about they that they be call common the devil land and be fear and avoid of all sea traveller alive above any other place in the world yet it please our merciful God to make even this hideous and hate place both the place of our safety and mean of our deliverance and hereby also I hope to deliver the world from a foul and general error it be count of most that they can be no habitation for man but rather give over to devil and wicked spirit whereas indeed we find they now by experience to be as habitable and commodious as most country of the same climate and situation insomuch as if the entrance into they be as easy as the place itself be content it have long ere this be inhabit as well as other land thus shall we make it appear that truth be the daughter of time and that man ought not to deny every thing which be not subject to their discover our strength truck with we upon such hard condition that our savage spy governor may very well see their subtlety and therefore neither can well endure nor will continue it and I may true say beside so have our man abase and to such a contempt have they bring the value of our copper that a piece which will have buy a bushel of baseness of our people their corn in former time will not now buy a little Cade or basket of a pottle and for this misgovernment chief our colony be much bind to the mariner who never yet in any voyage hither but have make a prey of our poor people in want insomuch as unless mischief of mariner they may advance four or five for one how assure soever of the payment of their bill of exchange they will not spare they a dust of corn nor a pint of beer to relation make by the lord de-la-warre to the lord and other of the counsel of Virginia touch his unexpected return home and afterward deliver to the general assembly of the say company at a court hold the twenty five of june 1611. publish by authority of the say counsel my lord etc. be now by accident return from my charge at Uirginia contrary either to my own desire or other man expectation who spare not to censure i in point of duty and to discourse and question the reason though they apprehend not the true cause of my return I be force out of a willingness to satisfy every man to deliver unto your lordship and the rest of this assembly brief but true in what state I have live ever since my arrival to the colony what have be the just occasion of my sudden departure thence and in what term I have leave the same the rather because I perceive that since my come into England such a coldness and irresolution be breed in many of the adventurer that some of they seek to withdraw those payment which they have subscribe towards the charge of the plantation and by which that action must be support and maintain make this my return the colour of their needless backwardness and unjust protraction which that you may the better understand I must inform your lordship that present after my arrival in james town I be welcome by a hot and violent ague which hold i a time till by the advice of my physician doctor Laurence b (...) n by blood let I be recover as in my first letter by sir Thomas g^^es I have inform you that disease have not long leave i till within three week after I have get a lord war many sickness little strength I begin to be distemper with other grievous sickness which successive and several assail me^ for beside a relapse into the former disease which with much more violence hold i more th^^ a month and bring i to great weakness the flux surprise i and keep i many day then the cramp assault my weak body with strong pain and afterward the gout with which I have heretofore be sometime trouble afflict i in such sort that make my body through weakness unable to stir or to use any manner of exercise draw upon i the disease call the scurvy which though in other it be a sickness of slothfulness yet be in i a effect of weakness which never leave i till I be upon the point to leave the World these several malady and calamity I be the more desirous to particularise unto your lordship although they be too notorious to the whole colony lest any man shall misdeem that under the general name and common excuse of sickness I go about to cloak either sloth or fear or any other base apprehension unworthy the high and honourable charge which you have entrust to my fidelity in these extremity I resolve to consult my friend who find nature spend in i and my body almost consume my pain likewise daily increase give i advise to prefer a hopeful recovery before a assure ruin which must necessary have ensue have I live but twenty day long in Virginia want at that instant both food and physic fit to remedy such extraordinary disease and restore that strength so desperate decay whereupon after a long consultation hold I resolve by general consent and persuasion to ship myself for Mevis a island in the west indies famous for wholsesome bath there to try what help the heavenly providence will afford i by the benefit of the hot bath but God who guide all thing according to his good will and pleasure so provide that after we have sail a hundred league we meet with southerly wind which force i to change my purpose my body be altogether unable to endure the tediousness of a long voyage and so steer my course for the western land which I no soon recover than I find help for my health and my sickness assuage by mean of fresh diet and especial of orange and orange and lemon good remedy for the scurvy lemon a undoubted remedy and medicine for that disease which last and so long have afflict i which ease as soon as I find I resolve although my body remain still feeble and weak to return back to my charge in Virginia again but I be advise not to hazard myself before I have perfect recover my strength which by counsel I be persuade to seek in the natural air of my country and so I come for England in which accident I doubt not but man of reason and of judgement will imagine there will more danger and prejudice have happen by my death there than I hope can do by my return in the next place I be to give account in what estate I leave the colony for government in my absence it may please your lordship therefore to understand that a honest and discreet english gentleman master rolfe and that after she have open renounce her country idolatry profess the faith of jesus Christ and be baptize which thing sir Thomas dale have labour a long time to ground in she yet notwithstanding be the virtuous deed of this worthy knight much debase by the letter which some wicked man have write from hence and especial by one c. l. if you hear any condemn this noble knight or do fear to come hither for those slanderow letter you may upon my word bold reprove thom. you know that no malefactor can abide the face of the judge but themselves scorn to be reprove do prosecute with all hatred all those that labour their amendment I marvel much that any man of honest life shall fear the sword of the magistrate which be unsheathe only in their defence but I much more muse that so few of our english minister that be so hot against the surplis and subscription come hither where neither speak of do they not either wilful hide their talent or keep themselves at home for fear of lose a few pleasure be there not any among they of Moses his mind and of the apostle that forsake all to follow Christ but I refer they to the judge of all heart and to the king that shall reward every one according to the gain of his talon but you my cousin hold fast that which you have and I though my promise of three year service to my country be expire will abide in my vocation here until I be lawful call from hence and so betake we all unto the mercy of God in Christ jesus I rest for ever part of a tractate write at Henrico in Virginia by master Whitaker minister to the colony there which then govern by sir t. dale 1613. they acknowledge that there be a great good God but know he not have the eye of their understanding as yet blind wherefore they serve the devil for fear after a most base manner sacrifice sometime as I have here hear their own child to he I have send one image of their god to the counsel in England which be paint upon one side of a toadstool much like unto a deform monster their priest who they call qui^kosoughs be no their priest and manner of live other but such as our english witch be they live naked in body as if their shame of their sin deserve no cover their name be as naked as their body they esteem it a virtue to lie deceive and steal as their master the devil teach they much more may be say of their miserable condition but I refer the particular narration of these thing to some other season these man be not so simple as some have suppose they for they be of body lusty strong and very nimble they be a very understanding generation quick of apprehension sudden in their dispatch subtle in their deal exquisite in their invention and industrious in their labour I suppose the world have no better marksman with their bow and arrow than they be they will kill bird fly fish swim and beast run they shoot also with marvellous strength they shoot one of our man be unarm quite through the body and nail both his arm to his body with one arrow one of their child also about the age of twelve or thirteen year kill a bird with his arrow in my sight the service of their god be answerable to their life be perform with a great fear and attention and many strange dumb show use in the same stretch forth their limb and strain their body much like to the counterfeit woman in England who fain themselves bewitch or possess of some evil spirit they stand in great awe of the quiokosough or priest which be a generation of viper even of Satan own brood the manner of their life be much like to the popish hermit of our age for they live alone in the wood in house sequester from the common course of man neither may any man be suffer to come into their house or to speak with they but when this priest do call he he take no care for his victual for all such kind of thing both bread and water etc. be bring unto a place near unto his cottage and there be leave which he fetch for (@) proper need if they will have rain or have lose any thing they have their recourse to he who coniur for they and many time prevail if they be sick he be their physician if they be wound he suck they at his command they make war and peace neither do they any thing of moment without he I will not be tedious in these strange narration when I have more perfect enter into their secret you shall know all final there be a civil government among they which they strict observe and show thereby that the law of yet Namantack in his return be kill in bermuda by another savage his fellow nature dwell in they for they have a rude kind of commonwealth and rough government wherein they both honour and obey their king parent and governor both great and less they observe the limit of their own possession murder be scarce hear of adultery and other offence severe punish the whole continent of Uirginia situate within the degree of 34. and 47. be a place beautify by God with all the ornament of nature and enrich with his earthly treasure that part of it which we already possess beginning at the bay of Chaesapheac and stretch itself in northerly latitude to the degree of 39 and 40. be interline with seven most goodly river the least whereof be equal to our river of Thames and all these river be so near join as that a^ 14. or (@) mile there be not very much distance of dry ground between either of they and those seu^rall main land be every where water with many vein or creek of water which sundry way do overthwart the land and make it almost navigable from one river to the other the commodity whereof to those that shall inhabit this land be infinite in respect of the speedy and easy transportance of good from one river to the other I can better manifest it unto you but in advise you to consider whether the water or land have be more beneficial to the low-countries to the river which we inhabit common call powhatans river ebb and flow one hundred and forty mile into the main at the mouth whereof be the two fort of Henrico and Charles two and forty mile upward be the first and mother-christian town seat call jamestowne and seventy mile beyond that upward be the new town of Henric^ build and so name in the memory of noble prince Henry of last and bless memory ten mile beyond this be a place call the fall because the river have there a great descent fall down between many mineral rock which be there twelve mile far beyond this place be there a crystal rock wherewith the indian do head many of their arrow three day journey from crystal rock thence be there a rock or stony hill find which be in the top cover all over with a perfect and most rich silver oar our man that go to discover those part have but two iron pickaxe with they and those so ill temper that the point of they turn again and bow at every stroke so that we can not search the entrails of the place yet some trial be make of that oar with good success and argument of much hope six day journey beyond this my a great ridge of high hill do run along the main land not far from who the indian report a great sea do run which we common call a south sea but in respect of our habitation be a west sea for there the sun set from we the high ground be much like unto the mould of France clay and sand be proportionable mix together at the top but if we dig any depth as we have do for out brick we find it to be red clay full of glister spangle there be many rocky place in all quarter and more than probable likelihood of rich mine of all sort though I know all yet it be not convenient at this time that I shall utter all neither have we have mean to search for any thing as we ought through present want of man and former want of provision for the belly as for iron steele antimonium and they have rather offer themselves to our eye and hand then be seek for of we the air of the country air and season especial about Henrico and upward be very temperate and agree well with our body the extremity of summer be not so hot as Spain nor the cold of winter so sharp as the frost of England the spring and harvest be the two long season and most pleasant the summer and winter be both but short the winter be for the most part dry and fair but the summer water often with many great and sudden shower of rain whereby the cold of winter be warm and the heat of summer cool many have die with we heretofore through their own filthiness and want of bodily comfort for sick man but now very few be sick among we not above three person among all the inhabitant of Henrico I will to God our soul be no sick than our body the natural people of the land be general such as you hear of before a people to be fear of those that come upon they without defensive armour but otherwise fainthearted if they see their arrow can pierce and easy to be subdue shirt of male or quilt cotton coat be the best defence against they there be but one or two of their petty king that for fear of we have desire our friendship and those keep good quarter with we be very pleasant among we and if occasion be serviceable unto we our elder friend be Pipisco and choapoke who be our overthwart neighbour at jamestowne and have be friendly to we in our great want the other be the werowance of chescheak who but late trade with we peaceable if we be once the master of their country and they stand in fear of we which may with few hand employ note well about nothing else be in short time bring to pass it be a easy matter to make fear be the begin of piety and civility what use may be make of the native they willing to forsake the devil to embrace the faith of jesus Christ and to be baptize beside you can easy judge how much they will be available to we in our discovery of the country in our building and planting and quiet provision for ourselves when we may peaceable pass from place to place without need of arm or Guard the mean for our people to live and subsist here of themselves be many and most certain both for beast bird and herb the beast of the country be for the most part wild as lion bear wolf and dear fox black and red rakown bever possown squerrels wilde-cat who skin be of great price and muskerat which yield musk as the musk-cat do there be two kind of beast among these most strange one of they be the female possowne which will let forth her young out of her belly and take they up into her belly possow a strange beast again at her pleasure without hurt to herself neither think this to be a traveller tale but the very truth for nature have frame her fit for that service my eye have be witness unto it and we have send of they and their young one into England the other strange condition creature be the fly squirrel which through the help of certain broad flappe of skin grow fly squirrel on each side of her foreleg will fly from tree to tree twenty or thirty pace at one flight and more if she have the benefit of a small breath of wind beside these since our come hither we have bring both cow goat and hog which prosper well and will multiply exceed if they may be provide for this country beside be replenish with bird of all sort which have be the best sustenance of flesh which our man have have since they come also eagel and hawk of all sort among who be ausprey fish hawk and the cormorant the wood be every where full of wild turkey which abound sort as swan flock of goose and brant duck and mallard sheldrake diverse etc. beside many other kind of rare and delectable bird who name and nature I can yet recite but we want the mean to take they the river abound with fish both small and great the sea-fish come into our river in march and continue until the end of September great scull Fish of herring come in first shad of a great bigness and SAMVEL purchas preacher of the word at the church a little within Ludgate London sir it be the nineteen of May before I be fit for my discovery when from Monahiggan I set sail in a open pinnace of five tun for the island I tell you of I pass alongst the coast where I find some ancient plantation not long since populous now utter void in other place a remnant remain but not free of sickness their disease the plague for we may perceive the sore of some that have escape who describe the spot of such as usual die when I arrive at my savage native country find all dead I travel alongst adays journey westward to a place call Nummastaquyt where find inhabitant I dispatch a messenger a day journey further west to Poconaokit which border on the sea whence come to see i two king attend with a guard of fifty arm man who be well satisfy with that my savage and I discourse unto they be desirous of novelty give i content in whasoever I demand where I find that former relation be true here I redeem a Frenchman and afterward another at who three year since escape shipwreck at the north-east of cape Cod. I must among many thing worthy observation for want of leisure therefore hence I pass not mention any place where we touch in the way to the island which we discover the twelve of june here we have good quarter with the savage who likewise confirm former report I find seven several place dig send home of the earth with sample of other commodity elsewhere find sound the coast and the time be far spend bare up for Monahiggan arrive the three and tie of june where we find our ship ready to depart to this i will be two other near adjoin all which I call by the name of king james his isle because from thence I have the first motive to search for that now probable passage which may hereafter be both honourable and profitable to his majesty when I have dispatch with the ship ready to depart I thus conclude for the accomplish my business in regard of the fewness of my man not be able to leave behind i a competent number for defence and yet sufficient furnish myself I put most of my provision aboard the Samson of cape Ward ready bind for Virginia from whence he come take no more into the pinnace than I think may serve our turn determine with god help to search the coast along and at Virginia to supply ourselves for a second discovery if the first fail but as the best action be common hard in effect and be seldom without their cross so in this we have our share and meet with many difficulty for we have not sail above forty league but we be take with a southerly storm which drive we to this strait either we must weather a rocky point of land or run into a broad bay no less dangerous etc. the rock we can not weather though we loose till we receive much water but at last be force to bear up for the bay and run on ground a furlong off the shore where we have be beat to piece have we not instant throw overboard our provision to have our life by which mean we escape and bring off our pinnace the next high water without hurt have our plank break and a small leak or two which we easy mend be leave in this misery have lose much bread all our beef and cider some meal and apparel with other provision and necessary have now little leave beside hope to encourage we to persist yet after a little deliberation we resolve to proceed and depart with the next fair wind we have not now that fair quarter among the savage as before which I take it be by reason of our savage absence who desire in regard of our long journey to slay with some of our savage friend at sawahquatooke for now almost every where where they be of any strength they seek to betray we at Manamock the southern part of cape cod now call sutcliffe inlet I be unaware take prisoner when they seek to kill my man which I leave to man the pinnace but miss of their purpose they demand a ransom which have I be as far from liberty as before yet it please God at last after a strange manner to deliver i with three of they into my hand and a little after the chief himself who see i weigh anchor will have leap overboard but intercept crave pardon and send for the hatchet give for ransom excuse himself by lay the fault on his neighbour and to be friend send for a canoas lade of corn which receive we set he free I be loath to omit the story wherein you will find cause to admire the great mercy of God even in our great misery in give we both freedom and relief at one time depart hence the next place we arrive at be capaock a island former discover by the english where I meet with epinew a savage that have live in England and speak indifferent good english who four year since be carry home be report to have be slay with diverse of his countryman by sailor which be false with he I have much conference who give i very good satisfaction in every thing almost I can demand time not permit i to search here which I shall have do for sundry thing of special moment the wind fair I stand away shape my course as the coast lead i till I come to the most westerly part where the coast begin to fall away southerly in my way I discover land about thirty league in length heretofore take for maine where I fear I have be embay but by the help of a indian I get to the sea again through many crooked and straight passage I let pass many accident in this journey occasion by treachery where we be compel twice to go together by the ear once the savage have great advantage of we in a straight not above a bow shoot and where a multitude of indian let fly at we from the bank but it please God to make we victor near unto this we find a most dangerous catwract among small rocky land occasion by two unequal tide the one ebb and flow two hour before the other here we lose a anchor by the strength of the current but find it deep enough from hence be we carry in a short space by the tide swiftness into a great bay to we so appear but indeed be break land which give we light of the sea here as I say the land tread southerly in this place I talk with many saluage who tell i of two sundry passage to the great sea on the west offer i pilot and one of they draw i a plot with chalk upon a chest whereby I find it a great island part the two sea they report the one scarce passable for shoald perilous current the other no question to be make of have receive these direction I hasten to the place of great hope where I purpose to make trial of God goodness towards we and use my best endeavour bring the truth to light but we be but only show the entrance where in seek to pass we be force back with contrary and overblow wind hardly escape both our life be thus overcharge with weather I stand alongst the coast to seek harbour to attend a favourable gale to recover the straight but be a harbourless coast for aught we can then perceive we find no succour till we arrive betwixt cape Charles and the main on the east side the bay chestapeak where in a wild road we anchor and the next day the eight of September cross the bay to Kecoughtan where the first news strike cold to our heart the general sickness over the Land here I resolve with all possible speed to return in pursuit of this business so that after a little refresh we recover up the river to james city and from thence to cape warde his plantacon where immediate we fall to hew of board for a close deck have find it a most desire course to attempt as before as we be thus labour to effect our purpose it please almighty God who only dispose of the time and season wherein all work shall be accomplish to visit we with his heavy hand so that at one time there be but two of we able to help the rest myself so sore shake with a burn fever that I be bring even unto death door but at length by God assistance escape and have now with the rest almost recover my former strength the winter have overtake we a time on these coast especial subject to gust and fearful storm I have now resolve to choose a more temperate season both for the general good and our own safety and thus I have send you a break discourse though indeed very unwilling to have give any notice at all till it have please God to have bless i with a thorough search that our eye may have witness the truth I have draw a plot of the coast which I dare not yet part with for fear of danger let this therefore serve for confirmation of your hope till I can better perform my promise and your desire for what I have speak I can produce at lest far separate of the sea behind they and of ship which come many day journey from the west and of the great extent of this sea to the north and south not know any bound thereof westward I cease to trouble you till a better opportunity offer itself remember my best loan etc. I rest from captain Martin his plantation 27. decemb. 1619. you to command tho. dermer to sir Edwin Sands in the treasurership succeed the right honourable Henry earl of Southampton cap. i. smith who industry together with that of those two brethren John and Nicolas Farrars the sir edw. Sands be treasurer from ap. 1619. till jun. 16^0 successive deputy have give much content to many but to diverse other matter of complaint wherein I be a unfit judge only as a reasonable man and christian minister that I say not historian I be much grieve that Virginia prosperity can answer man hope nor can any man marvel if division minde-massacre here with the massacre savage and disease there have hinder there the expect effect of honourable and careful endeavour master Stockam a master stockams letter to master Whitaker before minister write thence may the eight and twenty that which deserve just consideration that he find no probability by fair mean alone to draw the savage to goodness and if Mars and Minerva go hand in hand they will effect more good in one hour than these verbal mercurian in their life and till their priest and ancient have their throat cut there be no hope to bring they to conversion chap. 14 a true relation of a sea fight between two great and well appoint spanish ship or man of war and a english ship call thy Margaret and John or the black Hodge go for Virginia have take our journey towards Virginia in the begin of February last pass in a ship call the black Hodge her burden one hundred and sixty ton man 1620. only with eight iron piece and a poor falcon we soon over-passed both the tedious endurance and fearful danger of such a voyage and come at last by the fourteen of march under 13. and half latitude within twenty league of Matalina fall with Mevis by the twenty of march and compass the further point to stand in the hand summer with the shore we perceive two tall ship at anchor right over against the water place with their top sail loose and their boat go ashore for their man at first we suppose they hollander in respect of their building and the hollander colour bear by hollander colour their admiral in the main top the vice admiral have his fore top mast down and no colour display which increase our former opinion add withal that it must needs be prize or some other ship subject to the misfortune of a fight but drive by necessity of water and willing to refresh ourselves a shore we trim our ship and come to anchor fair by they send our boat in friendly manner to hale they both unprovided and unarmed which return with certificate that they be spaniard wherein not full satisfy by reason of our former apprehension that it be otherwise the better to be resolve we send out our boat again as well to be assure what to trust unto as to gain sometime to prepare our ship and trim she more commodious be pester with good and fardel between the deck and altogether unprovided for any fight either offensive or defensive the boat approach the hindmost ship which I call the vice-admiral and hale she demand who they be but instead of resolve we she command they to come aboard and will answer no otherwise whereupon the boat row from they as resolve all be not the spaniard shoot at the boat well and so make haste unto we again yet can not prevent a volley of small shot pour very dangerous among they insomuch that they have their clothes shoot through their oar shiver and the side batter with bullet yet thanks be to God neither be a man hurt nor any thing lose which as if they have have notice of the same escape rate their rage so much the more for by that time the boat be out of reach of their small shot they follow it to the ship with great ordnance and when they perceive they be safe come aboard they they shoot at the Ship english unprepared for fight take it so ill that they thunder against our ship with the soarer rage and most violent volley which we can not answer have no piece in our gunner room nor indeed any other well mount for such a sea fight by this time their vice admiral heave up her anchor to her warp and lay herself to spanish advantage windward if either we shall pass forward or anchor short again so that we perceive they mean to assault we on all hand for she let fly a whole broadside upon we and come furious up to our lee quarter without damage or resistance of our part but when we be thus terrify and threaten by they and thus encumber and disanimate among ourselves know withal by reason of our ill prepare ordnance the disadvantage and hazard to be board at anchor by two good ship well prepare for spoil and ruin we hoist up our sail and determine to set forward have not the vice-admiral come on our starboard side and beat upon we so hardly that we fall to our business and answer their unkndenesse according with many fair shot which prove most effectual especial from a demy-culuering which at last shoot she between wind and water so that she be compel from we and bear off to sea leave her admiral only single with we who at last come fair in our quarter to windward take in her holland flag and advance her spanish colour and so hale we spanish colour we quiet and quick answer both what we be and whither we be bind discover their conference the effect of our commission and relate the cause of our tarry there for water neither purpose to annoy any subject of the king of Spain nor by way of affront to brave either merchant or man of war then she charge we to strike our sail for the king of Spain and veil the bonnet according to the prerogative they have in those sea we reply with enlarge the particular of the league between the king our master and their king add with all that as we intend no ill we will take no wrong whereupon the master leave the poop and sequester himself from such open conference have they not call for the captain again who at last present himself till they command he to come aboard with his commission which he refuse yet wish they to send their boat aboard and then they shall see it most willing but instead either of answer we further with kind word or accept of our reply in good insolence of the spaniard part they make two great shot at we and pour among we such a volley of small shot before we can get off the poop that we thank God they do no more harm yet we be much amaze they do so much not thus content they wave we with their bright sword and revile we with opprobrious term mis-tearming we dog and invent more odious name against we than we can imagine that christian dare urge one another withal at last they lay we aboard which enforce we to raise up our main sail and to give the word to our small shot which all this while lie close well resolve and prepare but sudden break the english fight forth we ply they in such sort that we make they give back and shrink from their former forwardness the fight continue some half hour in our quarter and according to the terror of such encounter we be compass as it be in fire and smoke until they discover the waste of our ship naked and be encourage with the hope of reciprocal damage whereupon they brave run upon our side and lay we aboard loof to loof hasten with pike and sword to enter to which be add such fury that if they have not be prevent we shall have spaniard seek to enter shrink under the rage of a barbarous slaughter but it please God so to direct our master with advice and encourage our man with valour that our pike be former place under our half deck and certain shot lie close for that purpose under the portel of the ship encounter they so brave that their fury be not only rebate but their hastiness intercept their repulse and the whole company beat back especial upon the windward side where the charge be hot and the fight bloody for the^e the throng be great and man have work enough to make proof of their courage and fortune diverse of our man be hurt and many fall on their side in the end they be violent repulse by we enforce to a retreat until they be reinforce back again by their commander who stand upon term of honour as be man of war and design for that purpose think it a indignity to be so afront and countermand which cause a second charge and that be answer with a second beat back till the second charge captain himself grow enrage as not brook to be so much overmate and constrain they to come on a fresh which they do so effectual that questionless it have wrought a alteration three charge if the god that toss monarchy and tear the mountain in his fury have not teach we to toss our pike with prosperous event and pour out a sudden volley of small shot upon they whereby that worthy commander be slay at the foot of a pike and many of his soldier their captain slay drop down on the top of the hatch present our master take advantage of their discomfiture though with some commiseration for their valiant captain so slay that he not only ply they a fresh with great ordnance but have more false shot under the pike which be bestow to good purpose and amaze our enemy with the suddenness among the rest one Lucas our carpenter mate must not be forget who perceive a way how to annoy they as they be thus puzzle and in a confusion draw out a minion which he Lucas his brave act noble set a work under the half deck till at the last he bring it to the doxe of the half deck and there bend it upon they but in such a manner that when it be fire the case full of stone and piece of iron fall upon they like hail and clear their deck in such a sort that the case alter it slay many and in short time we see few assailant but only such as creep from place to place very covert and seem willing to obscure themselves from the fury of our shot which now be thick than they for although as far as we may commend our enemy they have do some thing worthy of admiration yet either want man or overtake with the unlooked for valour of our company they now begin to shrink and give we leave to be wanton with our advantage yet be our great ordnance only four that we can use in this fight but it shall seem the english can (@) but four ordnance they serve the turn as well as four time four for they shoot her diverse time between wind and water and so prevail that at last we see many sign of their willingness to leave we but by reason she be fast in a slach of our cable which in haste of weigh our anchor hang loose she can not be divide nor make that way she purpose until one of our man cut it with a axe without direction and be slay for his labour but when she perceive she be loose after she have be a board two hour and a half good lord what haste she make and how quick be we divide both great and small shot play on both side which last until spaniard fall off the remoteness be above a caliver shoot and we discover the vice-admiral come to her assistance who begin a far off to ply we with great shot and put we in mind we have another work in hand whereupon we man our ship a new separate the dead and hurt body by themselves bravado turn English from we and be so encourage that we wave she and in a manner make towards she to fight a fresh for when we perceive that the admiral make not a shot more at we we very imagine that either she be prepare herself with a new supply or want man to make her serviceable or resolve to go away from we consider she have lose her captain yet loath to be secure and imagine the vide-admiral may come and board we find we play till the admiral do make herself better ready we prepare ourselves wonder yet that she come no near we than Falcon shoot wherewith she ply we still on the lee side until at last she receive another payment from our demie-culuering which shoot she through and make she bear with the shore into smooth water where she remain till two of the clock after midnight and so we have time to reform our disorder and make ourselves better ready for the next day variety by break of day she come up again with the admiral with she as if they determine indeed next day fight to devour we at once but as it seem it be but a bravado though for the time they forsake not our quarter within musket shoot for all that night and morning they be quiet neighbour and keep we company without any great annoyance with their top-sail down not know as it shall seem what to do with we or else suspect their own hurt and leak they dare not trust themselves too far from land nor to the fury of another encounter all that night we have time and leisure to overlook our loss and prepare for they the admiral make show of a encounter and we after prayer be end provide to fight with they but sudden we perceive the vice-admiral hang a stern cut her main sail to come up and stir very ill at length the admiral shake in the wind and by apparent sign give we notice of slack her course whereby we may run a head and follow the sea at her pleasure so we perceive the vice-admiral seek to recover the island and the quality Sana the vice-admiral with all her sail to make towards a island call Sana which the admiral either take notice of as know the danger she wasin or give direction according consider there be no good to be do with we for present she tack about and lose we bear towards that island also we lose doctor Bohune and seven other be slay outright two die short after doctor Bohune and seven other slay outright of their wound and sixteen be shoot through in some part or other of the body who wound god be thank be recure and without maim or further impeachment of health be now recover and settle in Virginia according to our first intend purpose and commission I reckon not such as be hurt with pike and other offensive weapon because there be no danger in their cure and the skilful surgeon show his art and good speed with facility how many they lose we can tell nor what man of name be entertain among they only spanish loss I be sure we see many lie slay on the deck and more cast overboard in the fight beside the scupper run with blood and the very sea in their quarter be colour with a scarlet hue and look fearful upon we all the burden of their admiral be three hundred ton have two and twenty piece spanish ship describe of brass and all provision of a man of war indeed their vice-admiral three hundred tun and sixteen cast piece nor much inferior to she for trim and correspondent equipage and both to outward show over-masterfull and dare for one poor merchant and passenger be but a hundred and sixty ton have eight iron piece and one falcon overladen with Stuffe and ware encumber with passenger toil with a storm tire with a long voyage affright with want and every way insufficient to answer any such enemy but as it in the scripture it be all one to thou o God whether there be few or many and gedeon three hundred shall slay many thousand of the midianite as for deliverance the people of Israel shall pass through the red sea dry foot jonas shall be cast safe on shore out of the whale belly and Paul shall escape shipwreck save his life with in prepare as by the several declaration of each year in their particular manifest and approve in our general and public quarter-court and for the full satisfaction of all desirous to understand the treasurer master davison secretary etc. in the nine ship send in that fleet die but one passenger of seven hundred in who room there be another also bear at Sea their provision be not find so well own and thirty passenger well furnish the present gain by tobacco have make the plant of corn to be neglect and some think that if corn may there be value not at two shilling six penny the bushel as these part of Europe Orange and lemon-tree figtree sugar cane cotton-wool root that make very good bread Plantanes potato and sundry other indian fruit and plant not former see in Virginia which at the time of their say letter begin to prosper very well as also their indigo seed for the true cure whereof there be late cause a treatise to be write furthermore they write that in a voyage make by certain people of the mountain towards the south-west who get it from another nation beyond they some thirty day journey from patomacke call Acana Echinac be of small stature who have house apparel and household stuff like we and live within four day journey of the sea have ship come into their river and he his brother along with they to that king which offer the governor purpose not to refuse and the rather by reason of the continual constant relation of all those savage in Virginia of a sea and the way to it west they affirm that the head of all those seven goodly river the least whereof be great than the river of Thames and navigable above a hundred and fifty mile and not above six or eight mile one from another which fall all into one great bay have their rise out of a ridge of hill that run all along south and north whereby they doubt not but to find a safe easy and good passage to the south sea part by water and part by land esteem it not above a hundred and fifty mile from the head of the fall where we be now plant the discovery whereof will bring forth a most rich trade to cathay China japan and those other of the east indies to the inestimable benefit of this kingdom work the letter of the french vignerous or vine-man procure out of France and send over into Uirginia do likewise assertaine that no country in the world be more proper for vine french vignerous silk Rice o life and other fruit than Virginia be and that it far excel their own country of Languedocke the vine of diverse sort be in abundance natural over all the country they scarce believe those fruit to be grape till they have open they and see their kernel such be their bigness they be in love with the country and have plant some cut of vine at Michaelmas last in their letter affirm that these bare grape already this spring to their great wonder as be a thing they suppose not hear off in any other country a taste of wine make of the wild grape they last year send with hope to send a good quantity this next vintage and that the mulberry tree where they abide be in wonderful mulberry abundance and much excel both in goodness and greatness those of their own country of Languedocke and that those silkworm they have prosper exceed well and some silk they hope to send this year there want nothing to set up that rich commodity but store of hand wherewith England do abound of the fruit of which mulberry tree as of a plum there plentiful grow they will make wholesome drink for the colony and people there Opachankanough dote on a house which the english have build for he of our fashion he dwell therein show it to his own people and stranger with pride keep his key chary and busy himself with lock and unlock the door sometime a hundred time in a day admire the strangeness of that engine a lock and key he give the english leave to seat themselves any where on his river where the native be not actual seat and enter into further covenant of amity for reciprocal defence mutual transportation discovery of mine etc. they report also of copper piece present to Opachank which copper be gather at the foot of the mountain where they dig a hole in the ground in which they put the oar and make thereon a great fire which cause it to run into a mass and become malleable neither have they any tool but smooth stone for that purpose this seem strange to we which hear the english copper pass eleven fire his majesty gracious letter to the earl of South-hampton treasurer and to the counsel and company of Virginia here command the present set up of silk work and plant of vine in Virginia right trusty and well-beloved we greet you well whereas we understand that the soil in Virginia natural yreld store of excellent mulberry tree we have take into our princely consideration the great benefit that ma^ grow to the adventurer and planter by the breed of silkworm and set up of silkeworke in those part and therefore of our gracious inclination to a design of so much honour and advantage to the public we have think good as at sundry other time so now more particular to recommend it to your speciallcare hereby charge and require you to take speedy order that our people there use all possible diligence in breed silkworm and erect silkeworke and that they rather bestow their travel in compass this rich and solid commodity then in that of tobacco which beside much unnecessary expense bring with it many disorder and inconvenience and for as much as our servant John Bonoell have take pain in set down the true use of the silkworm together with the art of silkemaking and of plant vine and that his experience and ability may much conduce to the advancement of this business we do hereby likewise require you to cause his direction both for the say silkeworke and vineyard to be careful put in practice throughout our plantation there that so the work may go on cheerful and receive no more interruption nor delay give under our signet at our palace of Westminster the nine day of july in the twenty year of our reign of England France and Ireland and of Scotland the five and fifty WINDEBANK to our right trusty and right well-beloved cousin and counsellor henry earl of South-hampton treasurer of our plantation in Virginia and to our trusty and well-beloved the deputy and other of our say plantation Virginia the treasurour counsel and company of Virginia to the governor and counsel of state in Virginia reside after our very hearty commendation his sacred majesty out of his high wisdom and care of the noble plantation of Virginia have be gracious please to direct his letter to we here in England thereby command we to advance the set up of silkworke and plant of vineyard as by the copy herewith send you may perceive the intimation of his majesty pleasure we conceive to be a motive sufficient to induce you to employ all your endeavour to the set forward those two staple commodity of silk and wine which bring to their perfection will infinite redound to the honour benefit and comfort of the colony and of this whole kingdom yet we in discharge of our duty do again renew our often and iterate instruction and invite you cheerful to fall upon these two so rich and necessary commodity and if you shall find any person either through negligence or wilfulness to omit the plant of vine and mulberry tree in orderly and husbandly manner as by the book be prescribe or the provide of convenient room for the breed of worm we desire they may by severe censure and punishment be compel thereunto and on the contrary that all favour and possible assistance be give to such as yield willing obedience to his highness command therein the breach or performance whereof as we be bind to give a strict account so will it also be require of you the governor and counsel especial herein there can be no plea either of difficulty or impossibility but all the contrary appear by the natural aabundance of those two excellent plant afore-named every where in Virginia neither will such excuse be admit nor any other pretence serve whereby the business be at all delay and as we former send at our great charge the french vigneron to you to teach you their art so for the same purpose we now commend this book unto you to serve as a instructor to every one and send you store of they the book be print contain many good rule both for silk work vine and other husbandry but too long here to be insert to be disperse over the whole colony to every master of a family one silke-seede you shall receive also by this ship sufficient to store every man so that there want nothing but industry in the planter sudden to bring the make of silk to its perfection which either for their own benefit we hope they will willing endeavour or by a wholesome and necessary severity they must be enforce this particular advice we think necessary to give you lest that if it shall have come to you mingle with other you will have interpret it as a common instruction or a business that be not take so to heart as this by we and we hope will be by you in humble obedience to his sacred majesty royal instruction the pain and industry of the author for the benefit of the plantation be a member of our company be sufficient argument of his good affection to the action and they both deserve your best acceptance and we that other may thereby be invite to impart their knowledge in business of this and the like nature whereby the colony may not only be support for the present but bring to that perfection that may redound to the glory of God the honour of his majesty and the inestimable benefit of his noble kingdom which as they be the true aim and end the adventurer and planter have propose unto themselves so ought they to be still the honourable seed to put other also forward in this action we commend this business again to your special care and so we commit you all and your weighty affair to the protection of the almighty henry Southampton @. 3 the barbarous massacre commit by the savage on the English-Planters march the two and twenty 1621. after the english account the last may there come letter from sir Francis Wyatt governor in Uirginia which do advertise that when in November last he arrive in Virginia and enter upon his government he find the country settle in a peace as all man there think sure and unviolable not only because it be solemn ratify and swear and at the request of the native king stamp in brass and fix to one of his oak of note but as be advantageous to both part to the savage as the weak under which they be safe shelter and defend to we as be the easy way than think to pursue and advance our project or building plant and effect their conversion by peaceable and fair mean and such be the conceit of firm peace and amity as that there be seldom or never a sword wear and a piece seldom except for a deer or fowl by which assurance of security the plantation of particular hasty security adventurer and planter be place scatter and straggle as a choice vein of rich ground invite they and the further from neighbour hold the better the house general set open to the savage who be always friendly entertain at the table of the english and common lodge in their bedchamber the old planter as they think now come to reap the benefit of their long travel place with wonderful content upon their private dividend and the plant of particular hundred and colonies pursue with a hopeful alacrity all our project say he in a fair way and their familiarity with the native seem to open a fair gate for their conversion to Christianity the country be in this estate a occasion be minister of send to Opachankano the king opachankanoes dissimulation occasion by english security of these savage about the middle of march last what time the messenger return back with these word from he that he hold the peace conclude so firm as the sky shall soon fall than it dissolve yea such be the treacherous dissimulation of that people who then have contrive our destruction that even two day before the massacre some of our man be guide through the wood by they in safety and one Browne who then to learn the language live among the warrascoyack a province of that king be in friendly manner send back by they to captain hamor his master and many the like passage rather increase our former confidence than any wise in the world minister the least suspicion of the breach of the peace or of what instant ensue yea they borrow our own boat to convey themselves across the river on the bank of both side whereof all our plantation be to consult of the devilish murder that ensue and of our utter extirpation which God of his mercy by the mean of some of themselves convert to Christianity prevent and as well on the Friday morning the fatal day the two and twenty of march as also in the evening as in other day before they come unarm into our house without bow or arrow or other weapon with dear turkey fish fur and other provision to sell and truck with we for glass bead and other trifle yea in some place sit down at breakfast with our people at their table who immediate with their own tool and weapon either lay down or stand in their house they base and barbarous murder not spare either age or sex man woman or child so sudden in their cruel execution that few or none discern the weapon or blow that bring they to destruction in which manner they also slay many of our people then at their several work and husbandry in the field and without their house some in plant corn and tobacco some in garden some in make brick building saw and other kind of husbandry they well know in what place and quarter each of our man be in regard of their daily familiarity and resort to we for trade and other negotiation which the more willing be by we continue and cherish for the desire we have of effect that great masterpiece of work their conversion and by this mean that fatal Friday morning there fall under the bloody and barbarous hand of that perfidious and inhuman people contrary to all law of God and man of nature and nation three hundred and forty seven man woman and child most by their own 347. slay and base murder some think more weapon and not be content with take away life alone they fall after again upon the dead make as well as they can a fresh murder deface drag and mangle the dead carcase into many piece and carry some part away in derision with base and brutish triumph neither yet do these beast spare those among the rest well know unto they from who they have daily receive many benefit and favour but spiteful also massacre they one instance of it among too many shall serve for all that worthy religious gentleman master George Thorpe esquire deputy of the college he have write letter the year before may 17 testify the plentiful come up of the Cotten seed etc. attribute the ill success of thing to the not seek of God glory in convert the native which he say be peace able and want but mean indeed to murder they which this conceit procure sure bind sure find pity such a Abel shall be so Kai^ deceive land sometime one of his majesty pensioner and in one of the principal place of command in Uirginia do so true and earnest affect their conversion and be so tender over they that whosoever under his authority have give they but the least displeasure or discontent he punish they severe he think nothing too dear for they and as be desirous to bind they unto he by his many courtesy he never deny they any thing that they ask he insomuch that when these savage complain unto he of the fierceness of our mastiff most implacable and terrible unto they know they by instinct it seem to be but treacherous and false-hearted friend to we better than ourselves he to gratify they in all thing for the win of they by degree cause some of they to be kill in their presence to the great displeasure of the owner and will have all the rest have he not be hinder to make they the gentle and the mild to they he be not only too kind and beneficial to the common sort but also to their king to who he oft resort and give many present which he know to be high please to he and whereas this king before dwell only in a cottage or rather a den or hogsty make with a few pole and stick and cover with mat after their wild manner to civilize he he first build he a fair house according to the english fashion in which as before be say he take such joy especial in his lock and key which he so admire as lock and unlock his door a hundred time a day he think no device in all the world be comparable to it thus insinuate himself to this king for his religious purpose he confer after with he oft and intimate to he matter of our religion and thus far the pagan confess move by natural principle that our god be a good God and better much than they in that he have with so many good thing above they endow we he tell he if he will serve our god he shall be partaker of all those good thing we have and of far great than sense or reason ever can imagine he win upon he as he think in many thing so as he give he fair hear and good answer and seem to be much please with his discourse and in his company and both he and his people for the daily courtesy this good gentleman do to one or other of they do profess such outward love and respect unto he as nothing can seem more but all be little regard after by this viperous brood as the sequel show for they not only wilful murder he but cruel and felly out of a devilish malice do so many barbarous despite and foul scorn after to his dead corpse as be unbefitting to be hear by any civil ear one thing I can omit that when this good gentleman upon his fatal hour be warn by his man who perceive some treachery intend to they by these hellhound to look to himself and withal run away for fear of the mischief he strong apprehend and so save his own life yet his master out of the conscience of his own good meaning and fair desert ever towards they be so void of all suspicion and so full of confidence that they have soon kill he than he can or will believe they mean any ill against he at the time of this massacre there be three or four of our ship in james river and one in the next river and daily more to come in as three do within fourteen day after one of which they endeavour to have surprise but in vain as have also be their whole attempt have any the least foreknowledge be in those place where the massacre be commit yet be the heart of the english ever stupid and avert from believe any thing that may weaken their hope of speedy win the savage to civility and religion by kind usage and fair converse among they he and the whole counsel write further that almighty God they doubt not have his great work to do in this tragedy and will thereout draw honour and glory to his great name safety and a more flourish estate to themselves and the whole plantation there and the more speedy conversion of the child of those savage to himself since he so miraculous preserve so many of the english who desire to draw those people to religion by the careless neglect of their own safety seem to have be the great cause of their own ensue destruction yet it please God to use some of they as instrument to save many of their life who soul they have former save as at james city and other place and the pinnace trade in pamounkey river all who life be save by a convert indian convert Indian disclose the plot in the instant these wild naked native live not in great number together but disperse and in small manner of the savage life company and where most together not above two hundred and that very rare in other place fifty or forty or thereabouts and many mile distant from one another in such place among the wood where they either find or may easely make some clear plot of ground which they employ whole in set of corn whereby to sustain their life these small and scatter company as I have say have warning give from one another in all their habitation to meet at the day and hour appoint for our destruction at all our several town and place seat upon the river some be direct to go to one place some to another all to be do at the same day and time which they do according some enter their house under colour of truck and so take advantage other draw our man abroad captain Nathaniel Powel and his wife daughter of master William tracy and great with child and captain maycocke all gentleman of birth virtue and industry and of the council there suffer under this their cruelty and treason that the slaughter have be universal if God have not put it into the heart of a indian belong to one Perry to disclose it who live in the house of one pace be urge by another Indian his brother who come the night before and lay with he to kill pace so command by their king as he declare as he will kill Perry tell further that by such a hour in the morning a number will come from diverse place to finish the execution who fail not at the time perry Indian rise out of his bed and reveal it to pace that use he as a son and thus the rest of the colony that have warning give they by this mean be save such be God be thank for it the good fruit of a infidel convert to Christianity for though three hundred and more of we die by many of these pagan infidel yet thousand of we be save by the mean of one of they alone which be make a christian bless be God for ever who mercy endure for ever bless be God who mercy be above his justice and far above all his work who wrought this deliverance whereby their soul escape even as a bird out of the snare of the fowler pace upon this discovery secure his house before day row over the river to james city in that place near three mile in breadth and give notice thereof to the governor by which mean they be prevent there and at such other plantation as be possible for a timely intelligence to be give for where they see we stand upon our guard at the sight of a piece they all run a way in other place that can have no notice some piece with munition the use whereof they know not be there carry away and some few cattle also be destroy by they and as fame divulge not without probable ground their king have since cause the most part of the gunpowder by he surprise to be sow to draw therefrom the like increase as of his Maiz or corn in harvest next and that it be since discover that the gunpowder swoon practise before in captain smith time last summer Opachankano practise with a king of the eastern shore no guiltiness and fear of revenge see ship still come thither and weary of their watch and manifold loss and danger Opachankanough the author of the massacre be say to have come to his end by mean more these distract with a sudden remove and distress want it be think that 1800. survive both his majesty not a little move with the loss of so many his good subject and some complaint also be make of the government many of the virginian company here hold no such uniform agreement as be meet both show his gracious bounty in the gift of diverse arm out of the tower with further promise of his assistance and appoint commissioner to examine the cause of Virginia not answer to the care and cost in so long time bestow on she I be no fit relater of thing ensue and farre-unfit umpire in such difference I Summer call summer land the occasion you have before relate by master Strachie sup. cap. 6. and that some of their company take up their abode there this be not the first time that english eye have see those land for in the year 1593. Henry May have be there one of captain Lancaster company which have be in the east indies and in return have put over to trinidad and thence to puerto rico and hispaniola for refresh where captain Lancaster desire a Frenchman de Barbotiere to give this Henry may passage home with he they depart from laguna the last of November and December the seventeen be wrack on the northwest part of bermuda about midnight the pilot make themselves at noon to be twelve league to the southwards of the island certify the captain that they be from all danger and demand their wine of height which they have think they have be cast away by the shore but be seven league off by the help of their boat and a raft six and twenty of above fifty be save I say May dare not press in but stay in the ship almost full of water till the captain be enter the boat call i to he and I enter leave the better half of our company to the mercy of the Sea we row all day till a hour or two before night yet we can come on land tow the raft with the Boat have be all day without drink we seek long and at last one dig among weed find fresh water be only rain water which be all we find it please God that we have save our carpenter tool and go round to work we build a bark of some eighteen tun for the most part with trunnel and a few nail for tackle we make a voyage to our ship and cut down her shroud in stead of pitch we make lime and mix it with the oil of tortoise assoon as the carpenter have calk spread it on with a stick which be soon dry by the heat be in April we haste away for fear of water fail we we make two great chist and calk they and stow they on each side our main mast and so put in our provision of rain water and thirteen live tortoise for our food the hog be lean and there be store of fowl fish and tortoise there be also good fish for pearl the eleven of may we be clear of the land for our voyage to Newfoundland and on the twenty fall with the land near to cape Briton and thence to the bank of Newfoundland where a bark of Falmouth take we in wherein I have passage home and arrive at Falmouth in August 1594. thus much for may. let we now hear the relation send from a english colony plant there under the government of master Richard Moor this follow discourse have be print and be add to a tractate of master Silvester jordan touch the wrack of sir Thomas gate and sir George Summer on
